articles.title: F1 2019: How to watch the new Formula 1 season with Race Control
articles.summary: Race Control, broadcasting every track session of the new season, is available to Sky F1 subscribers on all devices through the Sky Sports App
articles.body:
It has never been easier to watch Formula 1 on the move thanks to Race Control on the Sky Sports App.

Race Control is available to Sky F1 subscribers on all devices through the Sky Sports app and will broadcast every minute of Formula 1 2019's track action.

To get into the driving seat for the new season, all you have to do as a Sky F1 subscriber is add the Sky Sports App to your phone:

iOS users: Download the Sky Sports App from the App Store
Android users: Download the Sky Sports App from the Play Store

What is Race Control?
Race Control is the digital version of the Sky Sports F1 channel with goodies attached.

In addition to providing a live stream of the Sky F1 channel during race weekends, users can also access the pit lane channel, onboard cameras, live data, and videos of on-track highlights.

In other words, it's up to you whether you want to use Race Control for its enhanced features, or as a second-screen experience, or use it for a live stream of Sky F1 when you're out and about.

You can enjoy Race Control on your iPhone, iPad, Android Phone or tablet and what's more - you can also stream the action from throughout the EU! You do not need to do anything differently, there are no additional steps or requirements, simply watch the action as you would when at home.

I'm a Sky Sports customer but don't have the Sky Sports app. Where do I get it?
You do not have to be a subscriber to download the Sky Sports App from the App Store - although only Sky F1 subscribers can access Race Control.

Get Sky Sports F1 - the home of every race weekend LIVE in 2019.

But Sky Sports subscribers and non-subscribers can also then create a Sky login to enable you to choose your favourite sports, teams, stars and experts, receive notifications for breaking news and your favourite sports.

I'm a Sky Sports customer with the Sky Sports app. Will I be logged in automatically?
Not the first time you launch the app, but you will stay logged in each time you open it. It's really simple to log in using your Sky username and password and it means you can watch Sky Sports channels, F1 Race Control, Premier League clips, choose your favourite sports, teams, stars and experts, receive notifications for breaking news and your favourite sports.

I can't remember my Sky Sports iD. How do l find it?
Just follow the 'Forgotten username or password?' links on the log-in prompt to retrieve or reset your details.

Will Race Control only be available for Sky Sports F1 customers?
Yes, Race Control is exclusively available to Sky Sports F1 customers.

What network mode strength will be required?
Race Control will play with whatever connection the user has. But the stronger the connection, the better quality of the Race Control streams.

Will I still be able to watch Sky F1 on the Red Button and Sky Go?
Yes. Sky F1 will still be available on Sky Go and our Red Button service, accessed via your TV screens, will be similarly unaffected.

Sky Sports F1 is the home of live and exclusive F1. Find out more here to watch the 2019 season live

articles.title: Black History Month: Sara Misir changed career after fracturing her skull and was first female Caribbean to race for Formula Woman
articles.summary: Sara Misir shares her inspiring journey through motorsport, bouncing back after a serious accident to becoming a professional racer; Race car engineer Jahee Campbell-Brennan reveals his experience in the industry and the work he is doing to increase diversity with the Motorsport UK board
articles.body:
Sara Misir, the first Jamaican Formula Woman racer reveals her incredible story, discussing her unusual route into the sport, facing barriers, and advice to younger generations who want to follow her path.

Misir tells Sky Sports News how her career in motorsport racing started. "It has been a long journey. I started when I was four years old, actually in equestrian. And that was my first passion.

"It was my dream to go to the Olympics and I was training to head to the Pan American Games when I was 16-years-old. Unfortunately, I had a small accident, so I had a small change in sports," said the 24-year-old who spoke to Sky Sports News from Silverstone.

  • 'I'm happier than ever' - How Africa helped Hamilton find peace
  • Why do so few people from Black and Asian communities swim?
  • 'Ethnicities never been a barrier in RL - but we need to tell more stories'

She explains the shift from equestrian to motorsport following her tragic accident when she was 16-years-old and how she came back into sport after a recovery that took half a year. "I was training for the Pan American games and me and my horse were warming up one morning.

"We were doing our normal jumping routine, getting ready for competition. And he tripped over a jump and unfortunately, I was half off, so I jumped off and spooked him.

"He spun around and kicked up and I got kicked in the face by my horse. It was about a six-month recovery. I had dislocated my jaw and my skull was cracked in half."

She adds: "It was a traumatic event to get over. And with that, it was a nine-hour surgery. When I got to the hospital, it was an intense way to go from being a top athlete to just being able to make it down the stairs without having to take a break halfway."

The Formula Woman racer says she had her "jaw wired shut" and was on a liquid diet for five months.

Looking to build a career in professional equestrian, she took a step back from the sport after suffering another injury: "About seven months later I got back on the horse, and I started training again. Unfortunately, I got bucked off and broke my shoulder in half that same year."

Misir shares the moment she was introduced to Motorsport racing by her father: "So it was a lot in one year. And my parents looked at me and said, 'Let's just take a small break and just relax from this for a second.'

"So, my dad with a long history in motorsports, introduced me to go-karting, he said: 'Just try this in the meantime it's competitive, high adrenaline, you will love it.'

"And he was right. I instantly fell in love with it. I started go-karting, but it was a love-hate relationship because you imagine I was training horseback riding since four-years-old and I was training that my whole life."

She adds: "I was making podium finishes, traveling around South America representing Jamaica, and then all of a sudden I came into a brand-new sport at 18-years-old with people that have been racing since they were four or five years old that knew it all already.

"But I had a good support network, who were just pushing me to keep on going. And there were so many times that I wanted to quit.

"But, with that village around me, it really allowed me to get to where I am today."

Misir explained the thrill of pursuing a motorsport career: "It's the mental aspect of racing that I love, your head-to-head with people. It's almost like a chess game where you have to pick where to pass, pick how to do it. You have to look at your opponent, see if they're more aggressive and read how they drive.

"I love it because it doesn't matter if you're male or female. I understand that between men and women you have the genetic advantages as a male.

"However, in a race car, it's a mind game. It's more of who has the experience or who can read the track better or who can perform at peak performance and have that mindfulness and relaxation and focus."

Misir reveals the high-intensity impacts that motorsport has not only on your mind but on your body: "People say, 'you just sit in a car and drive.' And it's so much more than that, I've gone a race day where I've lost almost six pounds.

"I went to my nutritionist, and she told me I burned about 9000 calories in one day and that was without going to the gym.

"So, there's a lot that goes into it."

When asked how she balances her work, social and educational life, she said: "Honestly, that has been another big challenge for me because, in January this year I was in school doing my Master's. I had my routine, it was structured. I would go to Jamaica for the three or four races a year for the Jamaican championship and it was very calm.

"Then I went into Formula Woman, and I realised if I want to throw myself into this dream, I have to do it. All or nothing.

"So, I took a year off from school and I left my job and I told them, 'Listen, I'm going for it.'"

Misir is the first Caribbean motorsport driver in her field. She said: "As the first woman from the Caribbean to come out of that, it's been such an honour because I've had such an impression on people.

"When I go back to Jamaica, so many women, kids, and girls come to me and say: 'I want to race too.'"

"And they see that it's possible. Before there was such a stigma and it seemed impossible. And me being able to open the door and show the younger generation that just because it seems impossible it doesn't mean it is."

"If you always do what you can, you'll never be more than you are."

When asked what diversity in the sport is like, Misir said: "It's already such a hard transition to go as a woman into a male-dominated sport and to have to add diversity to that.

"It just makes it such a bigger obstacle. But I'm really hoping to show that it's not as intimidating as it looks. And yes, the racing world is like a shark tank. It can be, but it's nothing that's impossible. If you put your foot down, it will happen.

"I would have to say Lewis Hamilton is doing such an amazing job. I've always found him such a great person to follow behind and follow his steps. I have always admired him for his modesty, respect for others and gratitude and never losing where he has come from."

Misir shares her ambitions for the future. "I would love to get into the GT3 series and get further into my career, but my focus is mainly on the process right now and just working as hard as I can to make sure I'm learning every day," she adds.

"Start making the right decisions, find out what kind of education you need to get there, it's all about just not giving up."

Jahee Campbell-Brennan is a race car engineer who spoke to Sky Sports News about his journey through the industry from working at Ford to creating his own company.

Campbell-Brennan also mentioned some of the barriers when entering his motorsport career. He said: "So when I realised I wanted to have a bit of a turn in my career and head into motorsport there were several barriers, such as some universities being more favoured by the industry.

"There's always that problem where you're only as good as your CV. So having spent some time in the automotive space and then wanting to work in vehicle dynamics and aerodynamics, which is what I specialise in, there was a lot of times where because it wasn't on my CV, even though I'd done lots of training and preparation for myself, I was kind of running into barriers in that sense."

How did he overcome those barriers?: "That is still a work in progress. I'm quite far from where I want to be in the long term.

"So it's just about getting yourself into the right spaces, having the right conversations. Obviously, with engineering you're never going to know everything.

"So, there's a lot of continued professional development, it's just a sort of a process that I think when you're determined enough, you will keep stepping in the right direction."

Having previously worked for Ford, he also faced the challenge of moving from working at a big company to taking on the challenge of creating his own business.

"That was an interesting transition. So, I used to contract there and after about four years, it kind of came to an end.

"For a while before that I'd had some thoughts about wanting to make a change but didn't really know how to do it. So, given my experience and having faced a lot of the barriers that people behind me will continue to face, I've not overcome them all, but I've got a good understanding of them and the best solutions for them."

The Lewis Hamilton Commission report published in 2021 stated: "The case for diversifying motorsport is clear and the time for change is now." After helping to work on this report Campbell-Brennan has put together a framework to identify some of the reasons why there is a lack of diversity in motorsport.

"I'm working with Motorsport UK on their racial diversity committee to consult them on the initiatives that would be effective at that level."

He also told Sky Sports News on the importance of representation: "It is a big thing because if you can see someone who looks like you, sounds like you, thinks like you, it can really inspire you to want to be like them."

articles.title: Indy 500: Josef Newgarden claims back-to-back triumphs after final-lap drama
articles.summary: Josef Newgarden secured victory in the 'Greatest Spectacle in Racing' for the second year running after coming out on top in a last-lap battle with Pato O'Ward; the American became the first driver for 22 years to win back-to-back at Indianapolis
articles.body:
Josef Newgarden won a final lap duel with Pato O'Ward to become the first back-to-back winner of the Indianapolis 500 in 22 years on Sunday.

Newgarden's victory capped an eventful afternoon at the Brickyard that saw the start delayed by four hours due to severe storms and the race interrupted by multiple cautions.

Yet the drivers managed to get in all 200 laps around the 2.5-mile oval, but only just with the race finishing in the Indiana sunset right before the 8.15pm (1.15am GMT) curfew.

  • Stream every F1 race with NOW Sports Month Membership
  • Get Sky Sports F1 | Get Sky Sports on WhatsApp

Newgarden gave the crowd of over 300,000 an American winner on the US Memorial Day weekend holiday. Chip Ganassi Racing's Scott Dixon was third.

"I'm just so proud of this team," Newgarden, who took a $440,000 bonus for winning back-to-back Indy 500s, said. "They crushed it - crushed it."

Starting on the front row alongside polesitter Scott McLaughlin and 2018 Indy 500 champion Will Power, Newgarden ran near the front of the pack all day.

But at the end the fight came down to the last-lap shootout with O'Ward, Newgarden sweeping past the Mexican's Arrow McLaren to become just the sixth driver to win back-to-back 500s and the first since Helio Castroneves in 2001 and 2002.

Newgarden's triumph marked team owner Roger Penske's 20th win of the 'Greatest Spectacle in Racing', albeit coming with a whiff of scandal.

Even as Newgarden celebrated chugging from the traditional quart of milk he took a moment to hit back at critics who have labelled him a cheat after his victory at the season-opening IndyCar race in St Petersburg was forfeited for illegal use of the push-to-pass feature that gives drivers a horsepower boost.

An investigation by team owner Penske, who also own the IndyCar series and the Indianapolis Motor Speedway, resulted in Newgarden's disqualification and sanctioning of several officials including the race outfit's president Tim Cindric and race engineer Luke Mason.

"They can say what they want, I don't even care," Newgarden said. "We worked our tails off.

"Luke, Tim, they're not here today but they are a huge part of this."

Formula 1 leaves Europe for the final time before the summer break as the championship moves on to Montreal for the Canadian Grand Prix. articles.body: No es la primera vez, ni será la última, que Red Bull o su 'equipo B',  ahora Racing Bulls, saque con cajas destempladas a alguno de sus pilotos. Liam Lawson ha sido el último en sufrir la gestión implacable de Helmut Marko... pero antes ha habido otros como él que lo han vivido. Uno de ellos es, además, un piloto español. Jaime Alguersuari también tuvo que salir de Toro Rosso no de las mejores maneras, precisamente. En su caso no fue a media campaña, sino tras completar la temporada 2011. Le comunicaron que continuaría... pero no sucedió. El catalán sabe lo que exige Marko a sus pilotos... que a veces es más incluso de lo razonable.  En una entrevista en la página oficial de la F1, Alguersuari ha salido en defensa del neozelandés, que correrá el próximo Gran Premio de Japón en Racing Bulls, dejando su asiento en el equipo Red Bull a Yuki Tsunoda. "Liam es nuevo, no conocía el coche, no conocía al equipo, no conocía las pistas, así que había que darle un poco de tiempo". “No lo ha hecho tan mal como parece. Era de esperar que sufriera al principio y que mejorara con el devenir de la temporada. No puede pasar de ser un héroe al peor piloto en sólo dos carreras", razonaba el catalán.  Alguersuari conoce las complejidades de la F1 actual y sabe que hace falta tiempo para dominarlas, especialmente cuando se cambia de equipo: "La F1 se basa ahora en pequeños detalles. Por ejemplo, tienes que poner los neumáticos en la ventana de funcionamiento o de lo contrario no tienes agarre, y puedes perder cuatro o cinco décimas muy fácilmente. Si miras los onboards de Liam en Australia y China, puedes ver que estaba luchando por el agarre en todas partes", explica. Sea cual sea la causa del fracaso de Lawson, Alguersuari empatiza con lo que está viviendo ahora el piloto kiwi: "Me trae recuerdos. La F1 se ha vuelto muy psicológica. Recuperarse de eso es sólo cuestión de fortalecer la cabeza. Tienes que entender que antes no eras un mal piloto. Liam necesita volver a sentirse cómodo dentro del coche, trabajar con los ingenieros, trabajar con el equipo, encontrar el ritmo que le faltaba e intentar llegar paso a paso". En el caso, además, de correr para Red Bull ahora que Verstappen es la referencia de la Fórmula 1 la dificultad para cualquiera es doble... como bien han experimentado pilotos del nivel de Daniel Ricciardo o Checo Pérez: "A lo largo de 24 carreras nadie va a ir más rápido que Max Verstappen en ese equipo. Es, probablemente, el mejor piloto que ha corrido nunca en la Fórmula 1. Su habilidad para pilotar un coche subvirador o un coche sobrevirador está en otra dimensión. Está por delante de todos", asegura el catalán. Alguersuari también salió al paso de los que argumentan que el Red Bull está hecho a la medida del tetracampeón del mundo: "Hay muchos rumores que dicen que el coche está hecho para Max, pero el coche está hecho para ser lo más rápido posible. Cada piloto tiene un estilo de conducción y Max es agresivo y le gustan los coches puntiagudos, porque un coche puntiagudo es siempre el coche más rápido".  "Max entiende y sabe muy bien cómo configurar ese coche para que se adapte a su estilo de conducción, y quienquiera que pongas en el otro coche está perdido, porque no puede conducir este coche con la misma configuración porque tiene demasiado agarre en la parte delantera. Entonces, si quitas ese agarre delantero, eres más lento, porque hay demasiado subviraje...", una encrucijada que se ha comido en los últimos años a Albon, Gasly, Ricciardo, Pérez, Lawson... y que ahora tendrá que vivir Yuki Tsunoda.  Alguersuari también se refirió al papel del japonés, que juega con cierta ventaja respecto a Lawson... y no precisamente porque tenga más experiencia: "Yuki no tiene nada que perder. Nadie espera mucho de él, así que superar esas malas expectativas será bastante fácil para él". El español cree que la oportunidad le puede haber llegado en un buen momento al nipón: "Ahora es un piloto muy sólido, que saca el máximo de su coche. El año pasado hizo un gran test con Red Bull en Abu Dhabi, y no le dieron el asiento. Probablemente esté en su mejor momento así que no debería sentir tanto la presión", concluyó. Además, debutar en su casa será una ventaja adicional: "Conoce la pista a la perfección, viene de hacer carreras sólidas y estará muy motivado por subir al equipo principal". Todo ello le hace pensar a Alguersuari que incluso podría estar cerca de Verstappen: "Me sorprendería si fuese mucho más lento que Max. Estará un poco por detrás, pero no creo que más de medio segundo o seis décimas", vaticina Pero lo mejor es que la referencia de Lawson será fácilmente superable, en teoría, para el japonés. "Hacerlo mejor que Lawson será algo muy asequible, aunque eso no quiere decir que me parezca justo que le bajaran. Si podrá mantener el asiento...nunca se sabe. Al menos está en una mejor posición que cualquiera de los pilotos junior en los últimos años", concluyó.

articles.summary: "Quiero acabar en el podio", recalca el sustituto del fulminado Liam Lawson con vistas a su primera carrera con la escuadra de Milton Keynes en la cita en Suzuka
articles.body: max Verstappen tendrá un nuevo compañero en Suzuka. Red Bull fulminó en la semana de receso entre la cita de China y la siguiente de Japón a un Liam Lawson que se ha quedado sin asiento en el primer equipo de la escudería de Milton Keynes en lo que dura un parpadear de ojos. Han bastado dos grandes premios para que los severos rectores (con Helmut Marko como buque insignia) hayan decidido ejecutar al neozelandés, quien deberá reconstruir su reputación en Faenza (formará pareja con el debutante Isack Hadjar en el Visa Cash App Racing Bulls). El elegido para intentar poner las cosas difíciles al número 1 actual del Gran Circo no es otro que Yuki Tsunoda. El nipón ha tenido que esperar bastante hasta haber encontrado una rendija por la que colarse en la escuadra energética. Han sido 89 grandes premios (contabilizando los disputados con AlphaTauri y Racing Bulls) hasta alcanzar la tierra prometida. Tsunoda es el sexto vecino de garaje de Mad Max. La lista es larga y con reputadas figuras de la categoría reina del automovilismo: Carlos Sainz, Daniel Ricciardo, Pierre Gasly, Alex Albon, Checo Pérez y el recién defenestrado Lawson. Pues bien, el '22' no es de los que enarbolan la bandera de mantener un perfil bajo. Con vistas a su estreno con Red Bull (y con el plus de que el tercer gran premio de 2025 se corre en su jardín), Tsunoda alberga la esperanza de hacer vibrar a los suyos... desde la zona noble del trazado nipón. "Siendo sincero, nunca esperé correr para Red Bull en el GP de Japón. Este año es el último de la alianza entre Red Bull y Honda, así que correr en Suzuka con ellos parece cosa del Destino. Todo ha cuadrado para que yo esté aquí hoy. Estoy muy feliz de estar en Red Bull, lo he pensado con detenimiento y correr para ellos en Japón parece producto de un sueño", confiesa en unas declaraciones recogidas por Motorsport.com. Y agrega henchido de emoción: "No quiero subir mucho las expectativas, pero para este Gran Premio de Japón, quiero acabar en el podio. Dicho esto, sé que no será nada fácil. Mi prioridad es entender el coche, ver cómo se comporta en comparación con el Racing Bulls. Si puedo disfrutar y familiarizarme con el RB21 en los Libres 1, sé que los resultados llegarán y si eso conduce a un podio, sería increíble". Lo que es evidente es que el competidor de 24 años da por hecho que lo va a hacer bien. "Pasé dos días en el simulador para adaptarme al nuevo monoplaza. A partir de esa experiencia, no me pareció que el coche fuera tan difícil de pilotar. Tengo la impresión de que la parte delantera responde mucho, como la gente dice, pero si me preguntas si es difícil de manejar, no diría que me ha dado una sensación particularmente extraña, como mínimo en el simulador", remacha.

articles.summary: Mario Andretti asegura que el piloto mexicano es una "opción" para el asiento de Cadillac en la temporada 2026 de la Fórmula 1
articles.body: Mario Andretti, campeón de la F1 en 1978 y director de la junta directiva de Cadillac, conversó en el podcast de 'ESPN Racing' sobre el futuro de General Motors en la categoría reina del deporte motor. De igual manera, el ex piloto estadounidense habló sobre el segundo asiento de la escudería para la temporada inaugural en el que salió a relucir Sergio Checo Pérez, a quien categorizó como "opción" para el puesto.  La fábrica de automóviles estadounidense recibió la aprobación formal de parte de la Fórmula 1 para entrar al deporte como el undécimo equipo de la parrilla para el año siguiente. Inicialmente se unirá con una asociación de tren motriz con Ferrari antes de convertirse en un equipo de trabajo de GM en 2028. Ahora, con el regreso de Liam Lawson a 'Racing Bulls', tras un pésimo comienzo de temporada con la escuadra de las bebidas energéticas, los rumores sobre el piloto mexicano no han parado de crecer. De igual manera, Andretti se hizo cargo de establecer una comparación entre sendos competidores.  "Bueno, me gustaría poder decírtelo, pero esto es algo que nosotros mismos mantenemos en secreto porque no queremos crear esperanzas en algunos ámbitos en los que podría no suceder", indicó el campeón estadounidense sobre su posible pareja de pilotos. "Así que creo que es muy importante que mantengamos esto entre nosotros hasta que se tome una decisión final. Hay muchos [pilotos] en Estados Unidos, ya sabes, pero debido a las licencias y todo lo demás, definitivamente no hay demasiadas opciones". Sin embargo, al hablar de su segundo piloto, Andretti se decantó por alguien con experiencia. "Pero el segundo piloto, el segundo asiento, será definitivamente un piloto experimentado que podría estar disponible. Y todos sabemos que la selección en ese sentido está bastante clara. Puede haber tres pilotos para elegir. Tres pilotos, siendo realistas, para elegir. Y no te voy a decir cuáles", esclareció el director de la junta directiva de Cadillac. Es aquí cuando hace su aparición el mexicano, puesto que Andretti lo catalogó como una opción. "Es una opción. Podría ser una opción. Por supuesto. Todo lo que puedo decir es que Liam Lawson está haciendo que Checo parezca muy, muy bueno". Andretti también ha insinuado anteriormente que el piloto de IndyCar Colton Herta podría ser un "gran candidato" para el equipo Cadillac.

articles.summary: El programa completo para que no te pierdas nada de la tercera cita del Mundial de Fórmula 1 2025
articles.body: Tras las citas de Australia y China, el Mundial de F1 recala en Japón. Del 4 al 6 de abril se disputar el tercer gran premio del curso 2025. En Suzuka recuperamos la normalidad. En Shanghái hubo formato Sprint, pero eso no se repetirá en el trazado nipón. La gran novedad con vistas a este tercer evento del año es el movimiento que ha tenido lugar en Red Bull. La escudería de las bebidas energéticas ha decidido poner en su primer equipo a Yuki Tsunoda para acompañar a Max Verstappen. El japonés corre en casa, por lo que tendrá una motivación en su gran estreno a los mandos del RB21. El gran damnificado de esta drástica decisión de los rectores del conjunto con base en Milton Keynes ha sido Liam Lawson. El neozelandés ha sido degradado a las primeras de cambio. Habrá que ver cómo rinde con RB tras descender en el escalafón de la estructura austriaca. Por lo demás, Lando Norris se presentará en el país del sol naciente como indiscutible líder del certamen. Saca 8 puntos al tetracampeón Verstappen, cuya pericia al volante del bólido energético está ocultando la debilidad de un bólido que no está a la altura de las poderosas armas con decoración naranja papaya. Por otro lado, Fernando Alonso y Carlos Sainz intentarán hacer olvidar su mal inicio del campeonato en Suzuka. Ni el de Aston Martin, ni el de Williams han tenido el favor de la diosa Fortuna en los dos grandes premios anteriores. El Gran Premio de Japón de Fórmula 1 2025 se podrá ver en TV en la plataforma de DAZN F1 y en Movistar +. También, tienes la opción de seguir todo lo que suceda en la carrera en el Circuito de Suzuka en directo a través de MARCA.com y Radio MARCA. Viernes 4 de abril: Entrenamientos Libres 1 (FP1): 4:30 - 5:30 horas. Entrenamientos Libres 2 (FP2): 8:00 - 9:00 horas. Sábado 5 de abril: Entrenamientos Libres 3 (FP3): 4:30 - 5:30 horas. Clasificación: 8:00 - 9:00 horas. Domingo 6 de abril: Carrera: 7:00 horas (58 vueltas).

articles.title: Felix Rosenqvist wins Indy 500 title after thrilling last-gasp overtake
articles.summary: Felix Rosenqvist overtook David Malukas in a dramatic final lap to win the 110th running of the Indianapolis 500 after becoming a new dad earlier this month; watch every F1 race live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Felix Rosenqvist swung to the outside of David Malukas, then found a way past the Team Penske driver to win the closest Indianapolis 500 in history by a margin of 0.0233 seconds on Sunday.

Malukas looked like he was in position to win when he passed the race leader Marcus Armstrong off the final restart with one lap to go while Rosenqvist and Armstrong, team-mates with Meyer Shank Racing, fought wheel to wheel down the back straightaway and through the fourth and final turn.

But Rosenqvist had just enough power to pull away from Armstrong and snake behind Malukas before making the decisive outside pass in the final 50 feet.

  • F1 2026 standings | F1 2026 Calendar | F1 Gossip Column
  • Download the Sky Sports app for expert analysis, best video & more📱
  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract on NOW📺

"What a car. Massive thanks to the team," Rosenqvist said. "We had two cars in the wind at the end and that's a luxury position to be in as a team.

"I felt we had the best car today. In all situations, we kind of had it all under control. That last yellow didn't help us, but it kind of worked out the right way when I got back to third, and then I had a flat-out lap on the high line, and it was just the coolest."

The closest previous finish came in 1992 when Al Unser Jr beat Scott Goodyear across the yard of bricks by 0.043 seconds.

It was Rosenqvist's second career win in 120 IndyCar races and comes after the recent birth of his first child. He is the third Swedish driver to win the race.

"I really miss my wife and my newborn child. I wish they were here," he said.

"I still don't believe it, becoming a dad and winning the 500. Maybe you'll win the 500 and have a baby. It's just unreal. Good job to Marcus and David at the end, they raced really cleanly - and because of those guys you get really good races.

A teary-eyed Malukas said: "I don't know what else we could have done. We were the fastest car in that whole race. We gave it 150 per cent. I almost crashed this car every lap. I'm sewn up with the P2. I don't know what else I can give.

articles.title: Hungarian GP: Martin Brundle on 'relentless' Lando Norris, Oscar Piastri-Carlos Sainz incident and Malaysia return to F1 calendar
articles.summary: Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle's verdict on Lando Norris' impressive Hungarian Grand Prix triumph, the Oscar Piastri and Carlos Sainz incident, plus the announcement Malaysia will host the Bahrain Grand Prix in early October
articles.body:
The Hungarian Grand Prix was an entertaining way to finish the first part of the 2026 F1 season before the summer break. The top four or five runners were often all visible in the same camera shot, and that included drivers from all four front running teams.

Lando Norris was on brilliant form and took both pole position and the victory, but not without a serious fight in both respects. It wasn't one of those days where a driver leads every lap from pole position and takes fastest lap. Oscar Piastri seized the lead in the second corner of the race, and Charles Leclerc in his Ferrari secured fastest lap but could only muster a fourth-place finish, and that would have been fifth had Lewis Hamilton in the sister Ferrari not attracted yet another penalty, this time for speeding in the pit-lane by 0.1kph.

It turns out Lewis did release the speed limiter a fraction early in order to beat Kimi Antonelli, who was on track, to the all-important safety car line which crosses the entire track and which decides who has the right to be in front, the driver exiting the pits, or the driver on track. It was declared that Antonelli was there a fraction earlier, and so Hamilton had to yield anyway. It was a pivotal moment for the final podium place and therefore the decision that speeding in the pitlane was a potentially competitive advantage was correct, however small the margin.

  • Mercedes driver scout Gwen Lagrue to join Red Bull as Helmut Marko replacement
  • F1 2026 standings | F1 2026 Calendar | F1 Gossip Column

  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract on NOW📺

Relentless Norris and unfortunate Piastri

Norris was on the radio saying that he was faster than team-mate Piastri in the lead, without specifically asking to be let through. Then he asked to pit first, but the pit wall rightly denied that as team protocol is that the leading of the two drivers has first option on stopping.

It was beginning to look like Norris' slide wide in Turn 2 and handing the lead to Piastri would cost him a victory. McLaren pitted Piastri on Lap 16 to cover off the pit stops from Hamilton and Verstappen, and Norris next lap around on Lap 17.

But it was the second round of stops on this high tyre wear circuit that made the difference. Piastri pitted on Lap 33 again to cover Hamilton on fresh tyres, and then Norris had his chance to prove he was indeed faster by running hard and pitting on Lap 39, giving him a decent tyre life offset to his team-mate Piastri.

Through the latter stages of the race lapped drivers appeared to be slow or even reluctant to clear the way for the leaders coming through, and it turns out there was an issue with the blue light warning system. That does still leave mirrors and team radio though.

On that same Lap 39, Piastri was coming up to lap Carlos Sainz's Williams who was having his own battle with fellow countryman Fernando Alonso, and after running wide in the infamous Turn 2 which had given Piastri the lead on the opening lap, and which must have looked for all the world to Piastri that he'd seen him and was letting him through, just as Sainz swung heavily back to the racing line and clashed with the race leader.

Sainz had been informed by his Williams team but his position on the outside of a 180 degree turn meant he had no mirror sight of Piastri tight on the inside, and so his penalty was mitigated down to five seconds, which was zero comfort to a rightly angry Piastri.

Piastri did well not to spin out but he lost crucial time and Norris would emerge from the pits into a lead he would not relinquish. In fact, he would relentlessly increase it despite a third stop under a Virtual Safety Car for fresher soft compound tyres on Lap 56 to recover, so painfully, Piastri's McLaren which had suffered transmission failure.

The young Australian hasn't been able to catch any kind of lucky break for the best part of a year now.

Verstappen fights off Ferraris

Max Verstappen spent much of the race complaining about aerodynamic degradation, poor handling, and inconsistent gear shifting with his Red Bull, but would finish in a fine second place after some impressive overtakes on Hamilton's Ferrari. Max thought Lewis was a bit tough on him in the braking zone, but he wasn't.

It was explained to me that if the Red Bull has any damage on the aero parts particularly underneath the car, on an aggressive kerb for example, this has a disproportionate affect on the overall downforce and so grip. Hence Max's aero degradation comment.

Ferrari had looked the team to beat throughout practice, and most folk in the paddock thought they were favourites even though Norris pipped them to pole. Hamilton had smartly saved a brand new set of soft tyres by clearing the first stage of qualifying on medium tyres. These would have been extremely handy from his front-row grid slot, but he attracted a three-place grid drop from a rather brutal but unintentional blocking of another driver who was on his final qualifying attempt. You'll not be surprised to read the blocked driver was Piastri.

Leclerc fluffed his qualifying with a delete lap time for track limits, and had only managed to save a set of lightly used soft tyres to start the race with. You may remember that Ferrari humbled the entire pack from the start down to the first corner in the earlier races of the season, but such is the development curve in this business, even with a tyre advantage, Hamilton only made up one place on the opening lap and Leclerc, starting on the right hand and dirtier side of the grid, fell from the front row to fifth. And now they had to manage those soft tyres and following other cars, and so their race was immediately compromised.

Ferrari would try to help Hamilton with relatively early stops on Laps 13 and 30 for the speed of fresh tyres. But with Verstappen's combative prowess this paid no dividends. Ferrari pitted both drivers again under the Lap 56 Virtual Safety Car for fresher soft tyres but that only served to allow Antonelli to get ahead (as explained earlier), a position he would keep to the final podium spot.

Mercedes curiously off the pace

Having dominated this season so far, Mercedes were curiously off the ultimate pace, and a three-place grid penalty for Antonelli for failing to sufficiently lift for yellow warning flags in qualifying when Verstappen spun in the final corner, meant that he had lined up seventh, one place behind team-mate George Russell who was also struggling for pace.

George had also collected some engine damage with a run over the kerbs in Turn 4 and would need a new power unit fitted for race day. Whether all this new kit was responsible for a truly awful start is not so far certain, but Toto Wolff seemed clear it was a car issue.

Everything on a racing car, and especially a Formula 1 car, is positioned as low as absolutely possible to lower the centre of gravity, and so helping the handling through corners, and this leaves components vulnerable.

Russell would drop all the way back to 21st and begin a long afternoon fighting back to seventh place, tantalisingly close to Isack Hadjar's Red Bull in sixth.

Antonelli would secure that podium to increase his championship lead to 50 points over Hamilton heading into the break, and 59 points over his team-mate Russell. That's very much the definition of 'damage limitation' from seventh on the grid in such a competitive field on a circuit notoriously difficult for overtaking.

Liam Lawson would finish a fine eighth and Arvid Lindblad 10th for Racing Bulls to move them up into a fifth in the Constructors' Championship ahead of Alpine. What a happy and cohesive team that appears to be.

And Nico Hulkenberg scored two points for Audi in ninth. In my mind's eye, so far this season I think of Audi consistently around and inside the top ten on pace, but actually they are eighth of 11 teams in the championship, underlining that with an improvement in reliability they can be strong contenders in the relentless midfield battle in the second half.

Aston Martin made a decent jump in performance with a comprehensive aero upgrade, and apparently leapfrogging Cadillac and Williams, and threatening Haas, all at once, but they along with Honda still have a long way to go. Nonetheless it was finally encouraging for the Silverstone team.

Championship far from over

If McLaren have made a decent upgrade step which translates well to other circuits, this was the team's 14th Hungaroring victory, and with the top four are ever closer, this championship is far from over. There are still 291 points available assuming all the remaining races take place given the Middle East conflict.

On that subject, the Bahrain GP will now be run at the very popular Sepang circuit in Malaysia. This is the same impressive lateral thinking and flexibility F1 and its partners showed during the pandemic and I applaud it.

It sounds as if there will definitely be a European replacement race in late November or early December if Qatar and Abu Dhabi can't take place. We may need to fit some headlights and wipers for that race but the teams and drivers will handle it in their stride as usual.

I wish you all a happy summer break.

MB

articles.title: Kevin Doyle: Former Premier League striker chasing Cheltenham Festival glory with Augusta Kate and La Bague Au Roi
articles.summary: Reading, Wolves and Republic of Ireland striker Kevin Doyle now runs Slaney River Stud in Wexford, where he has former Grade One-winning mares Augusta Kate and La Bague Au Roi; watch Unbridled On Tour on the At The Races YouTube channel
articles.body:
Former Premier League striker Kevin Doyle would rather breed a Cheltenham Festival winner than relive the best goal of his career.

Since retiring from football, the Republic of Ireland international has been focused on creating the next generation of jumps racing stars, with considerable success already.

Having purchased Grade One-winning mares Augusta Kate and La Bague Au Roi, Doyle's Slaney River Stud has already produced multiple winners.

  • Diamond Necklace sparkles in Nassau Stakes
  • Bow Echo roars home late to seal Sussex Stakes success

Doyle's interest in horses and the breeding industry came from his father Paddy, who bred Cheltenham Festival winner Holywell at the family stud. Now, Kevin is hoping he can follow in his father's footsteps.

The Unbridled podcast duo of Matt Chapman and Paddy Brennan are on tour this summer and headed over to Ireland to visit the former Reading and Wolves goalscorer.

"This is what gets me up in the morning now," Doyle explained. "I want a Cheltenham Festival winner now. I've done that [scoring goals]. That's an easy answer.

"Cheltenham is the one you want on the CV. If Holywell was bred here, why not another one?

"You have to hope, horse breeding is just hope. You're doing your best, you have all your routines, but who knows? It's a tough game."

Asked which of his former team-mates he would take with him to Cheltenham for a day out, Doyle added: "John O'Shea. He knows his horses and he'd have the craic and a few pints.

"We were in a syndicate together when we were players and John was the organiser but it wasn't the most successful! The one time a horse we had won, we didn't know it was running!"

Doyle has just over 20 horses on his 40-acre farm, including a Poet's Word colt out of Augusta Kate and recently sold a two-year-old Crystal Ocean gelding out of Augusta Kate to Noel George and Amanda Zetterholm in France.

Dual Grade One winner La Bague Au Roi is also a promising broodmare prospect for Doyle, having survived a freak life-threatening injury at the yard.

articles.title: Goodwood: Evening Saigon continues magical week for Wathnan Racing with Stewards' Cup win as Goodie Two Shoes also prevails
articles.summary: Evening Saigon crowned a memorable week at Glorious Goodwood for the Wathnan Racing team when taking out the Saturday feature, the Stewards' Cup in the hands of their number-one rider James Doyle; Goodie Two Shoes won the Qatar Lillie Langtry Stakes
articles.body:
James Doyle picked the right one from three choices as his bosses at Wathnan Racing topped an amazing week at Glorious Goodwood with victory in the Coral Stewards' Cup with Evening Saigon.

The win was a feather in the cap for the owners, who target this fixture with a vengeance, but perhaps more telling it was a second major handicap of the week for Qatari-born trainer Hamad Al Jehani.

Having also won the Golden Mile with Archivist when Doyle picked the wrong one, Al Jehani was able to celebrate a famous victory with the whole team on this occasion.

Despite higher numbers being preferred at Thursday's draw, the finish was dominated by the eventual winner drawn in 10 beating Stratusnine in five. Jamie Spencer flew from the back on Mitbaahy for third but he was beaten a head and a short head. Completely Random was fourth.

  • Jim Crowley to retire from riding and start training
  • American Affair flies the flag for Goldie at Goodwood

"It's been a great week. Obviously I was very deflated last year with just one and we were really frustrated by that so the memo was we need to do better and that's everyone, including me as well," said Doyle.

"We've done a lot of work this week looking at different tactics and things like that, track position and stuff. All the guys back home in the office, these guys, Hamad has done an unbelievable job with this horse as well.

"He's not an easy conveyance, setting off he was that well in himself he tried to get rid of me the first few strides but that was great.

"We just had the perfect set-up. Dark Thirty was near me, I was able to draft in behind him and we didn't go that mad I didn't think for a Stewards' Cup so I was happy to pull him out before the two and set sail for home.

"I knew the second horse, I won on him the other day at York, he's a pretty decent horse too so it was a good tussle up to the line.

"Hamad and his team, it's nice that they have won the two big handicaps this week."

Al Jehani said: "I am very happy for Evening Saigon and very happy for the team. He performed very well at Royal Ascot and it was the right decision from the management to keep him for the Stewards' Cup.

"It's really important for us and it's a really important race for the season. I'm very happy and thanks to James for giving the horse a great ride.

"It's not easy to be competitive with the best trainers in the world but we try our best and I think we are building in a very good way, with great help from the management. Hopefully, we will improve year by year and we can make Wathnan be in the winner's enclosure more and more."

Wathnan's racing advisor Richard Brown added: "James had a bit of a hard choice but he was pretty firm on riding this lad in the end. Hamad has turned up and won two of the hardest handicaps to win all year. We plot these and work as a team - when these results come off, it's just fantastic for Wathnan and what Wathnan is all about.

"If you look at Hamad's statistics since he started training, they match up with the best trainers in the country. He's a phenomenal horseman and was a very good rider himself. He's very modest about it but he showjumped to a good level. He's a great horseman and he's formed a great team. We all work very closely together and to pull this off is huge for everybody involved."

Goodie Two Shoes sticks her neck out to edge Lillie Langtry battle

Goodie Two Shoes needed to be very brave as she added to Joseph O'Brien and Dylan Browne McMonagle's fantastic week at Goodwood in the Qatar Lillie Langtry Stakes.

With three winners already in the bag, the JP McManus-owned Goodie Two Shoes was sent off an 8/1 chance to bag a first victory of the season but looked to face a tough ask as Santorini Star kicked for home.

She still had ground to make up with 100 yards to the line but the seven-year-old stuck her neck out right where it mattered to get the verdict by a nose.

Goodie Two Shoes was second in the Melbourne Cup in November and a return to Australia will surely now be on the cards following this Group Two triumph.

The winning rider said: "She's a lovely filly, she's improving all the time since she started coming back this year, she's got better with each run.

"I was quietly confident she would get a lot closer to these fillies, she ran well last year [third] when the ground turned up soft but she would gallop down the road for you, she handles quick ground. I got a lovely split through them and she wanted to win.

"To be honest I didn't think I'd won but I looked back at the camera and she had her head stuck down for me at the right time; I did think Tom (Marquand) had won but we came out the right side of it.

"These are very, very special silks to put on. A big thanks to JP for putting me up and she's going to have a nice campaign through to the end of the season.

"I'm sure the Melbourne Cup is probably the main target, the boys will know that and Joseph and JP will discuss it but I'd probably guess that's the obvious target."

Sir Anthony McCoy, representing McManus, said: "I didn't think she had won but Jason Weaver said right on the nod, not before the line or after the line but right on the line, she put her head in the right place.

"She got a good ride - he was going to ride her for that bit of luck, down the inside, and he got a lot of luck. When you are as good as Dylan Browne McMonagle and you are riding for Joseph O'Brien, you seem to get a lot of luck.

"Dylan was over at mine a few times when he was 11 or 12. He is very mechanically correct, like Ryan Moore, and he's got that chip - that little thing where he could go the wrong way. I mean it in a good way. As Frankie found out one day at Ascot, he has that little edge to him.

"She was second in a Melbourne Cup and I thought she had been quite well handicapped for the Galway Plate if she ran there off 123. It's nice when you win races like this and hopefully she will be able to go back to the Melbourne Cup."

articles.title: Bow Echo: George Boughey's unbeaten star miler in shock retirement from racing after setback
articles.summary: Bow Echo retires a perfect six from six, winning three Group One races this season, earning him comparisons with the great Frankel; George Boughey has called it "the honour of a lifetime" to train Bow Echo
articles.body:
Bow Echo has been retired from racing after the shock news that George Boughey's unbeaten star has suffered a setback in training.

Having won the 2000 Guineas, the St James's Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot and the Sussex Stakes this season, Bow Echo was being lined up for Sunday's Prix Jacques le Marois.

Announcing the surprise news on his X account, Boughey said: "It is with great disappointment that we have to announce that Bow Echo has had a setback and will be retired from racing.

  • 'Exciting' Sun Goddess looks the part in Phoenix Stakes
  • Moore helps GB and Ireland to Shergar Cup crown

"It has been the honour of a lifetime to train a horse like Bow Echo. He has given us some extraordinary days and taken everyone involved on a journey we will never forget.

"To retire unbeaten, having won the 2000 Guineas, St James's Palace Stakes and Sussex Stakes says everything about what an exceptional racehorse he has been.

"Bow Echo's remarkable story began with his owner-breeder, the late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid and it is a great sadness that he was not here to see what a lifetime of breeding was able to produce.

"Bow Echo's unbelievable constitution and extraordinary ability have set him apart. We will all miss seeing him at home and on the racecourse but we are incredibly excited for his next chapter and in time, to see a new generation of his progeny on the racecourse."

articles.title: Crouch guides Coppull home in Hungerford to complete big-race double
articles.summary: Coppull completed a valuable double for Hector Crouch and the Clive Cox team at Newbury on Saturday with a dominant display in the Group Two Hungerford Stakes
articles.body:
Coppull stepped up in distance to land a second Group Two of his career under an enterprising ride from Hector Crouch, who completed a big-race double in the Visit Malta Hungerford Stakes at Newbury.

The three-year-old Clive Cox-trained colt finished third in the July Cup last time out but a bold plan to move up to seven furlongs was landed in fine style for his jockey, who also completing a treble on the card.

Crouch delivered Coppull in eyecatching style, too, peeling away from the main group towards the far side two-and-a-half furlongs from home at the head of a three-strong breakaway, a path which proved quicker to the line.

It proved a masterstroke as the Bated Breath colt stayed on too strongly to land the £93,571 pot by one-and-a-quarter lengths at 15-2 from Prince Of India (14-1) with a further three-quarters of a length back to another of the breakaway trio, the 5-2 favourite Symbol Of Honour.

  • 'Exciting' Sun Goddess looks the part in Phoenix Stakes
  • Unbeaten star Bow Echo in shock retirement after setback

Cox, who was credited by Crouch with the decision to go far side, said victory over seven furlongs had given them options for the remainder of the season.

"He was unlucky not to be a place closer at least in the July Cup but he always gave me the impression he would stretch another furlong, even as a two-year-old where he ran so well in the Coventry," he told ITV Racing.

"He's got a lot of class and he reminds me an awful lot of Lethal Force who won this race back in 2012 and he went on to be champion sprinter the year after he won this.

"He's still quick enough for six furlongs and while I'm not convinced he likes it really soft, with the dry summer we've had we've got choices now.

"If he comes back all right we could still run in the Haydock Sprint Cup and that would be with a bit of confidence after today. And we still have the Park Stakes [Group Two over seven furlongs at Doncaster] which obviously he would have a penalty in."

Melbourne Cup next stop for Wine Dark Sea after Freer success

Wine Dark Sea made every yard of the running to land a gamble in the Highclere Thoroughbred Racing Geoffrey Freer Stakes at Newbury and set up a possible tilt at the Melbourne Cup.

Connections have recently sold a share in the four-year-old gelding to Australian Bloodstock and victory under Hector Crouch was enough to earn a place in the Flemington race.

Making all under Crouch, Wine Dark Sea, who was well backed from 13-2 into 7-2, never looked like being pegged back and stayed on well in the straight to pull clear of the staying-on Tabletalk to win by a length and a half.

William Haggas' 2-1 favourite Dubai Honour was a neck further back in third.

Winning trainer Harry Charlton confirmed the Melbourne spectacular was the next stop for the improving four-year-old with the horse set to go into quarantine on September 9.

"The intention today was to finish third which would help with the ballot qualification for the Melbourne Cup and he has done more than that," said Charlton.

"The Aussies who I'm dealing with were saying finish third and they won't change his handicap mark. It is very different how they do it."

Wine Dark Sea ran out an impressive winner of handicaps at Ascot and Carlisle earlier in the season but could manage only fifth when well supported at Newmarket's July meeting.

Charlton was inclined to put that disappointment down to the rigours of a stiff finish and long journey to the Cumbrian track.

"Although he won on the bridle at Carlisle he broke the track record carrying top weight so you can't have an easy race, particularly travelling eight hours in a heatwave. The 10 days later we just saw a slightly flat horse.

"My brother [Tom] trains in Australia and has a Melbourne Cup runner as well. I have a team going down with the horse and you train out of the quarantine barn at Ballarat."

articles.title: Deauville: Rayif roars back to his best to land Prix Jacques le Marois
articles.summary: Francis-Henri Graffard added yet another Group 1 crown to his collection when French 2000 Guineas winner Rayif battled to victory in the Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques Le Marois at Deauville.
articles.body:
French 2000 Guineas hero Rayif bounced back to form to repel a strong raiding party in the Aga Khan Studs Prix Jacques le Marois at Deauville.

Francis-Henri Graffard's colt struck Classic gold on what was his seasonal debut in the Poule d'Essai des Poulains in early May, but his summer campaign has been interrupted, with a planned visit to Royal Ascot scuppered by a minor setback after which he ran a little below par when fifth in the Prix Jean Prat.

He had plenty on his plate stepping back up to a mile, with Aidan O'Brien's Irish 1,000 Guineas and Coronation Stakes winner Precise the hot favourite after bumping into top-class older filly Blue Bolt on her last couple of starts.

Fozzy Stack's Prix Jean Prat victor Thesecretadversary took the field along for much of the way, closely pursued by Karl Burke's Zeus Olympios, who looked the likely winner after quickening to the lead inside the final furlong.

  • Rayif wins the Prix Jacques Le Marois | Race replay
  • Godolphin's Gold Cup hero Trawlerman retired

But Mickael Barzalona delivered Rayif with a withering late run and he got up to deny Zeus Olympios an elusive first Group One success, with Precise close up behind in third.

"I'm very happy, it's a wonderful race to win, a very hard race to win," said Graffard.

"I kept my confidence in the horse. He ran pretty well the other day with excuses and he was in top form (today). Over that course you need the perfect trip and we had the perfect trip today.

"He travelled really well and picked up really nicely, he's very tough and game.

"He won the Poule d'Essai on very soft ground so everyone was saying he's a soft ground horse, but you need to keep trying and if these horses are to find their place at stud they need to be performing at this level.

"The Jacques le Marois is a very famous race - probably the second most famous race in France after the Arc - so it's a wonderful race to win. It means so much."

Rayif has a range of options for the second half of the season, including the Queen Elizabeth II Stakes at Ascot on Champions Day, for which he was cut to 4-1 second-favourite from 14-1 by Coral.

Graffard added: "It depends if we decide to go for the Prix du Moulin (September 6) or give him more time and the Prix de la Foret (October 4) could be an option - I wouldn't be afraid to drop him back in distance.

"There is the QEII at the back-end and we know he can handle soft ground."

Of the gallant runner-up, Burke said: "We always thought and hoped he would produce that sort of performance in a Group One. I think physically he's improving and he showed that today.

"He quickened twice there - first time I thought we'd got it, then he got challenged and then he quickened again and I thought we'd got it and so did Cliff (Lee, jockey).

"The winner, fair play to him, has come and cut us down. Francis can do no wrong, can he?

"We'll get him home and see how he is. It's got to be discussed, but as a trainer I'm very hopeful he'll stay in training next year and I think he'll just continue improving physically and strengthening, so hopefully if he doesn't win his Group One this year he'll certainly get it next year.

"I'd say the race at Longchamp (Moulin) will probably come a bit quick for him, maybe we'll wait for the QEII at Ascot."

Fozzy Stack's Prix Jean Prat victor Thesecretadversary took the field along for much of the way, closely pursued by Karl Burke's Zeus Olympios, who looked the likely winner after quickening to the lead inside the final furlong.

  • Rayif wins the Prix Jacques Le Marois | Race replay
  • Godolphin's Gold Cup hero Trawlerman retired

But Mickael Barzalona delivered Rayif with a withering late run and he got up to deny Zeus Olympios an elusive first Group One success, with Precise close up behind in third.

"I'm very happy, it's a wonderful race to win, a very hard race to win," said Graffard.

"I kept my confidence in the horse. He ran pretty well the other day with excuses and he was in top form (today). Over that course you need the perfect trip and we had the perfect trip today.

"He travelled really well and picked up really nicely, he's very tough and game.

"He won the Poule d'Essai on very soft ground so everyone was saying he's a soft ground horse, but you need to keep trying and if these horses are to find their place at stud they need to be performing at this level.

"The Jacques le Marois is a very famous race - probably the second most famous race in France after the Arc - so it's a wonderful race to win. It means so much."

Rayif has a range of options for the second half of the season, including the Queen Elizabeth II Stakes at Ascot on Champions Day, for which he was cut to 4-1 second-favourite from 14-1 by Coral.

Graffard added: "It depends if we decide to go for the Prix du Moulin (September 6) or give him more time and the Prix de la Foret (October 4) could be an option - I wouldn't be afraid to drop him back in distance.

"There is the QEII at the back-end and we know he can handle soft ground."

Of the gallant runner-up, Burke said: "We always thought and hoped he would produce that sort of performance in a Group One. I think physically he's improving and he showed that today.

"He quickened twice there - first time I thought we'd got it, then he got challenged and then he quickened again and I thought we'd got it and so did Cliff (Lee, jockey).

"The winner, fair play to him, has come and cut us down. Francis can do no wrong, can he?

"We'll get him home and see how he is. It's got to be discussed, but as a trainer I'm very hopeful he'll stay in training next year and I think he'll just continue improving physically and strengthening, so hopefully if he doesn't win his Group One this year he'll certainly get it next year.

"I'd say the race at Longchamp (Moulin) will probably come a bit quick for him, maybe we'll wait for the QEII at Ascot."

articles.title: Oficial: Carlos Sainz renueva con Williams
articles.standfirst: El español firma un acuerdo multianual con los de Grove que le mantendrá en la estructura británica en el futuro inminente
articles.summary: El español firma un acuerdo multianual con los de Grove que le mantendrá en la estructura británica en el futuro inminente
articles.body: Todo hacía indicar, como venía contando MARCA desde hace varios días, que Carlos Sainz sólo pensaba en Williams y que su renovación sería inminente después de semanas de reunión y reflexión en el parón estival, y la primera ficha en el tablero de los británicos al confirmar que su compañero, Alex Albon, también continuaría. No ha habido dudas, el madrileño seguirá con el azul de Grove en un acuerdo multianual, sin especificar el curso de finalización como se viene haciendo en los acuerdos de la Fórmula 1 moderna. Sainz es uno de los activos más valiosos de la Fórmula 1 y su papel seguirá pasando por liderar a Williams. Fue vital en el subidón de 2025, con dos cajones de Gran Premio y uno sprint que rompían una sequía para los británicos desde Bélgica 2021 (aquella carrera del diluvio donde Russell aprovechó su posición de salida al no competirse). En la segunda mitad de la campaña alcanzó un nivel altísimo, permitiendo que los británicos fuesen el quinto clasificado en la parrilla de forma holgada. En 2026 la situación es menos feliz, pero el madrileño vuelve a levantar la mano para tratar de enderezar el rumbo de una fábrica que no aterrizó comprendiendo del todo bien qué requería la nueva era de la clase reina. En su defensa, pocas lo han podido hacer del todo. El acuerdo supone que Carlos Sainz va a cobrar entorno a los 30 millones de euros, según ha podido saber MARCA, con lo que entraría en un nivel que sólo tienen ahora cinco pilotos en la F1: Verstappen, Hamilton Leclerc y Lando Norris. Un estatus de alguien que tiene el nivel de campeón del mundo o que lo sería con el coche adecuado. Los salarios más altos de la F1 Al respecto, habría que corregir que Sainz no estaba en 13 millones, como se deba por buenos en el 'paddock', sino bastante más arriba, más bien cerca de lo 20. Williams habría mejorado su sueldo en un tercio, que es muy destacable. Sainz ha firmado por dos años, aunque tiene cláusulas de posible salida al final de la primera, algo que no le gustaría tener que ejecutar, ya que sería la demostración de que el proyecto camina después del terrible inicio de 2026. Además, ha habido conversaciones con otros equipos, pero el español tenía claro que no quería bajarse del barco de Vowles y Williams a la primera, ya que se siente muy identificado con esta misión de devolver a los de Grove a la cabeza que un día ejercieron en la F1. “Creo en el trabajo de este equipo, tanto en el circuito como la fábrica y la inversión a largo plazo. Tenemos que dar la vuelta a esto juntos. Sigo tan comprometido como el primer día, tratando de devolver a lo que pertenecen, y quiero seguir creando recuerdos juntos”, defiende Sainz en el comunicado oficial. Fiel a su mensaje, de trabajo y capacidad de cambiar a los equipos como siempre ha demostrado desde que se subió a un Toro Rosso, pasó por Renault y desembarcó en dos grandes, McLaren y Ferrari. Allí dejó huella y hace no mucho tiempo seguía ese mensaje en la Scuderia en el que se extrañaba el trabajo metódico del español. Algo que ni Leclerc, muy explosivo pero menos analítico que Sainz, ni Hamilton, que ha necesitado un coche a su medida para volver a rendir, logran. Son condicionantes que valoran, lógicamente en la estructura británica, con un James Vowles que siempre ha admirado al piloto español. “Desde que llegó Carlos, su talento fue muy valioso trabajando para el proyecto. Es un líder, y estoy ansioso de ver qué logramos juntos y lo posible de reconstruir. Carlos comparte nuestra ambición y empuja todos los días para ello. Somos un equipo capaz de pelear por cada gramo de rendimiento”, admite. A ello se unirá un salario de piloto estrella, algo que también es un mensaje sobre la nueva realidad de los británicos, con capacidad de atraer a mejores pilotos y patrocinadores que apoyen a su proyecto. La renovación de Sainz se oficializa, como se vive en los tiempos modernos de la Fórmula 1, sin apuntar a la fecha concreta de finalización del concreto. Partirá del 2027, irá al 2028 y cuenta con la capacidad de ejecutar cláusulas de rendimiento si se presentan oportunidades lejos de Williams. En este mercado se le vinculó a Audi, pero no pasó de un mero rumor, pues el ‘55’ y su entorno se centraban totalmente en las conversaciones con Williams. Allí seguirá en el corto plazo, buscando más competitividad tras el sinsabor del 2026. Que es una realidad que Sainz no ha dudado en admitir mientras ponía deberes a su equipo. El primer golpe dramático llegó al aterrizar tarde el invierno, empezar con un coche muy pasado de peso y tener que remontar. A ello se sumó que las actualizaciones recientes no arrojaron todos los beneficios que esperaban desde el túnel de viento. Todo ello se suma y deja un panorama en el que Williams querrá dar un salto más en Bakú y el foco pasará a ser 2027 pese a que el FW48 todavía pueda recibir algún tipo de retoque. En todo ese trabajo, Sainz es clave. Volviendo a liderar a los de Grove, manteniendo una velocidad a una vuelta y en carrera que es superior a la de su compañero Albon y luchando por resultados pese a que tiene que sobreponerse a una máquina que no está, de momento, a la altura de las manos del español. Su futuro sigue pintándose de azul. El 55 seguirá luchando.

articles.title: Sainz, renovación galáctica: "Tenemos todos los ingredientes para devolver a Williams a lo más alto"
articles.standfirst: El español relata a los medios oficiales del equipo británico su compromiso fiel con la estructura de Grove
articles.summary: El español relata a los medios oficiales del equipo británico su compromiso fiel con la estructura de Grove
articles.body: La gran noticia justo antes del regreso al paddock de la Fórmula 1 con motivo del Gran Premio de los Países Bajos, en el majestuoso Zandvoort, es la renovación de Carlos Sainz en el equipo Williams. No tanto por el hecho en sí, que parecía lógico. Y sí por una apuesta a lo grande. Que tiene que ver con un sueldo galáctico (cercano a 30 millones por curso), en el top-5 de la parrilla. Y una apuesta total para que el madrileño sea el que devuelva a los británicos a la zona alta. Ya lo hicieron en 2025, pasando del fondo de la parrilla a ser la quinta fuerza del campeonato. Y el 2026 arrojará una situación parecida que Sainz afrontará. "El objetivo es el mismo: devolver al equipo a donde pertenece. Será un camino duro, pero tenemos los ingredientes correctos para lograrlo. Si nos focalizamos en el proceso, los detalles y creemos en el instinto, estoy convencido de que llegarán los resultados. Es el desafío y estoy listo para ello", defendió en los medios oficiales del equipo. Sainz será en Zandvoort un protagonista clave tras un proceso en el que valoró qué era lo mejor para su carrera y sus objetivos internos. La respuesta fue seguir. "Hay razones para hacerlo. La principal, por la gente que forma esta familia, y creo en esa fuerza para ser exitosos. Tenemos el talento, la motivación y la pasión para devolver al equipo a lo más alto. Además, hay cambios, inversiones y proyectos ocurriendo que me hacen creer que vamos en lo correcto", añadió. Sin obviar lo evidente. "Este curso fue un bache en el camino, pero tenemos los ingredientes correctos para lograr salir más fuertes", explicó. En esos ingredientes parece que existen dos caminos clave. Uno es el trabajo interno del equipo para encontrar qué falla y cómo solucionarlo. "Sigo lo que ocurre de forma interna, tanto en pista como en la fábrica y los cambios que veo son excitantes. Es cuestión de tiempo que todo funcione junto, y ver los resultados en pista", detalló. Y se une una materia gris prometedora que encabeza James Vowles. "Una cosa que valoro mucho es la relación directa. Lo vivo con todos, es importante ser honesto y transparente, con un ambiente donde se tome responsabilidad de las decisiones que tomamos. Es el tipo de conversación que tenemos en este equipo", lanzó. Su reto será volver a pelear por objetivos importantes, como los dos podios de Gran Premio y el de sprint del 2025. "El sentimiento que tuve cuando crucé la meta en Bakú [su primer cajón] no puedo explicarlo con palabras. Siempre lo recordaré. Y hay otras cosas que la gente no ve y son destacadas, como encontrar soluciones cuando pasas un fin de semana sufriendo viendo que tu sensaciones en el simulador y el trabajo ha funcionado. Te hace sentir orgulloso y te hace sentir empujando", recordó. Así las cosas, la carrera del 55 seguirá teñido de azul. "Veo a Williams como una gran familia y los fans son muy importantes. Nos dan la inspiración y fuerza para que podamos hacerles sentir orgullosos. Sus mensajes y cánticos nos ayudan, tanto a mí como a todo el equipo. Y cuando visten el azul nos elevan tras días duros", cerró. Sigue creyendo. "Tenemos un camino largo por delante, pero nada me haría más feliz que llegar juntos al destino", cerró.

articles.title: Sainz renueva... ¿y Alonso?
articles.standfirst: El español de Williams se aseguró uno de los mejores contratos de la parrilla y el foco del futuro pasa a su compatriota que todavía no ha comunicado su decisión
articles.summary: El español de Williams se aseguró uno de los mejores contratos de la parrilla y el foco del futuro pasa a su compatriota que todavía no ha comunicado su decisión
articles.body: la primera ficha en el tablero de los españoles en la Fórmula 1 cayó con la renovación a lo grande de Carlos Sainz por Williams. Su nuevo contrato, de unos 30 millones por temporada, le dispara a los guarismos de otras estrellas de la parrilla, como el último campeón Lando Norris. Y deja al otro piloto que compite con la rojigualda en el casco, Fernando Alonso, con los focos colocados encima de su gran decisión. La de alargar una carrera deportiva que viene desde 2001 batallando en la élite y tiene las dos coronas (2005 y 2006) como joyas. Si bien es cierto que existieron voces que mezclaron su futuro en la parrilla, esas posibilidades no pasarán de rumores con un Sainz que no dudó de su continuidad en Williams tras semanas de debate con su entorno y el propio equipo británico. "Tenemos todos los ingredientes para volver a lo más alto", defendió tras estampar su firma en su nuevo contrato multianual. Por su parte, Fernando Alonso vive una situación similar, pues Aston Martin será la firma que acompañe su decisión. Esté en pista en el proyecto con Newey y Honda o decida dar un paso al costado. "Yo tengo contrato, sigo", contó. Los dos españoles son los líderes claros de sus proyectos deportivos y también se han encontrado con una parrilla que apenas mueve fichas o apuesta por otros nombres. Quizá el papel de animador de la silly-season corresponde a Alpine y Gucci -estructura vinculada a varios nombres de prestigio-, pero no es una escudería llamada a asaltar la zona alta. En Mercedes, Ferrari, McLaren y Red Bull, las cuatro dominadoras de la parrilla, los movimientos se antojan imposibles. Aunque Verstappen y su entorno agitan el avispero, los movimientos apuntan más a 2028 con nuevos contratos que volver a negociar. Así las cosas, por Alonso y Sainz pasará la reacción de sus equipos para llegar a la zona alta. En Williams existe fe en el proceso, mientras que Aston Martin formó un equipo de élite a velocidad de vértigo, pero se encontró con un inicio de 2026 para olvidar. Eso sí, no tiene que ver con la decisión de Alonso, que apunta a otros factores como el conjunto de normas de la F1. Pero es el mismo tablero para todos. "El reglamento es lo que los equipos o la federación piensan que es mejor; así que hay que sacar partido al coche para ganar carreras, estar arriba y pensar en el próximo reglamento cuando venga. Ahora es lo que tenemos y hay que hacerlo mejor", reconoció en las últimas carreras antes del verano. Eso sí, con el anuncio de Sainz queda su decisión como último gran punto culminante, más allá del rumbo final de Verstappen. En este 2026 no ha terminado de aclarar qué pasa por su cabeza. Sí pasó por una despedida adelantada en Montmeló, otros mensajes que parecían camino de la continuidad, y desemboca en un debate que todavía no tiene respuesta. O por lo menos, de cara al exterior. Quizá en Holanda arroje luz a su corto plazo en la F1.

En Mercedes, Ferrari, McLaren y Red Bull, las cuatro dominadoras de la parrilla, los movimientos se antojan imposibles. Aunque Verstappen y su entorno agitan el avispero, los movimientos apuntan más a 2028 con nuevos contratos que volver a negociar. Así las cosas, por Alonso y Sainz pasará la reacción de sus equipos para llegar a la zona alta. En Williams existe fe en el proceso, mientras que Aston Martin formó un equipo de élite a velocidad de vértigo, pero se encontró con un inicio de 2026 para olvidar. Eso sí, no tiene que ver con la decisión de Alonso, que apunta a otros factores como el conjunto de normas de la F1. Pero es el mismo tablero para todos. "El reglamento es lo que los equipos o la federación piensan que es mejor; así que hay que sacar partido al coche para ganar carreras, estar arriba y pensar en el próximo reglamento cuando venga. Ahora es lo que tenemos y hay que hacerlo mejor", reconoció en las últimas carreras antes del verano. Eso sí, con el anuncio de Sainz queda su decisión como último gran punto culminante, más allá del rumbo final de Verstappen. En este 2026 no ha terminado de aclarar qué pasa por su cabeza. Sí pasó por una despedida adelantada en Montmeló, otros mensajes que parecían camino de la continuidad, y desemboca en un debate que todavía no tiene respuesta. O por lo menos, de cara al exterior. Quizá en Holanda arroje luz a su corto plazo en la F1.

articles.title: Fin de la especulación: Verstappen renueva hasta 2030 con Red Bull
articles.standfirst: El neerlandés amplía su vinculación con el equipo de la bebida energética tras varios Grandes Premios de dudas
articles.summary: El neerlandés amplía su vinculación con el equipo de la bebida energética tras varios Grandes Premios de dudas
articles.body: Fin a la gran historia que podría mover las sillas principales del mercado de la Fórmula 1. Max Verstappen ha renovado con Red Bull y su vinculación ya no arroja ningún tipo de dudas, pues llegará a 2030 e igualará al contrato de Charles Leclerc con la Scuderia Ferrari como el más largo de la parrilla. Ni retirada, ni movimiento, el cuatro veces campeón seguirá fiel a los colores que le han dado todo en el Gran Circo. Verstappen ha vivido un 2026 con incógnitas relacionadas con su futuro. En Japón, una de las citas iniciales con el polémico nuevo reglamento, desveló que se pensaría que hacer con su carrera profesional al no sentirse cómodo con el devenir de la F1. Después se unieron rumores, lanzados desde su propio entorno, en los que había relación con McLaren. Pero la única realidad palpable es Red Bull y la ampliación le confirma como gran jefe de filas. Y se plantará en la nueva era, que iniciará entre 2030 o 2031, con capacidad de replantear su situación. “Estoy satisfecho por la extensión contractual. Tenemos el mejor equipo y estoy feliz por seguir juntos para volver a lo más alto. Es nuestro objetivo y lo seguimos persiguiendo. Quiero dar las gracias por la confianza que depositan en mi”, explicó Verstappen. Su anuncio llegó a pocas horas de que empiece la acción en Zandvoort, el Gran Premio de casa del cuatro veces campeón. Nada es casualidad y es el broche a una renovación que parecía cantada. En su foco seguirán los títulos entre ceja y ceja. “Vine al equipo queriendo ganar carreras, hemos logrado cosas increíbles y continuar mi etapa aquí es lo que siempre he querido”, cerró. Su nombre apareció vinculado a Mercedes y McLaren y relacionado a cláusulas de rendimiento, pero el neerlandés mantiene que sólo piensa en Red Bull. Y, lógicamente, Red Bull lo ve con orgullo. Su jefe de filas sigue allí. “Mantener al mejor piloto de la parrilla es una gran noticia para todos nosotros y también para el mundo del motor”, sentenció su jefe Laurent Mekies. Los asientos principales se cierran así. Así las cosas, Alonso es el único nombre estelar que falta por anunciar qué hará con su carrera deportiva en el largo plazo.
