articles.title: Aston espera a Alonso y llega la hora de Honda: "Cumple nuestro objetivo interno en fiabilidad y rendimiento"
articles.standfirst: El optimismo reina en el seno de los de Silverstone, con un futuro mejor tras las novedades en su unidad de potencia y creyendo en la continuidad de su estrella
articles.summary: El optimismo reina en el seno de los de Silverstone, con un futuro mejor tras las novedades en su unidad de potencia y creyendo en la continuidad de su estrella
articles.body: En Zandvoort, con la playa rozando cada curva del majestuoso carrusel holandés, la lluvia arrecia y amenaza con ser protagonista, por primera vez en mucho tiempo, de un Gran Premio. Pero en el seno de Aston Martin  sale el sol tras 11 carreras difíciles. Se liberaron, en cierta manera, al ver que sus mejoras aerodinámicas funcionaban antes del verano y en el Gran Premio de los Países Bajos suman el nuevo motor de Honda. Entre las renovaciones que han virado el foco del paddock, con Carlos Sainz y Max Verstappen como protagonistas, su paso adelante vuelve a tomar fuerza. Hasta se lo toman con cierta gracia. Su ingeniero jefe en pista y portavoz, Shintaro Orihara, aterrizó con un cartel en el que pedía a la prensa no preguntar por su potencia o los tiempos por vuelta. Aunque con MARCA presente sí que adelantaron que las novedades se harán notar. "No podemos explicar cuánto reducimos la diferencia y en la F1 no hay milagros, pero sí creemos que habrá pasos positivos. Existe diferencia con los demás rivales, pero hemos vuelto a la velocidad de competir con la actualización de Aston Martin. Cada décima será importante para mejorar la posición y esta actualización nos dará ese tipo de mejora", explicaba el japonés. En la tabla puede presentarse un horizonte mejor. Para ser un firme contendiente en la zona media que lideran los Racing Bulls. "En algunas pistas iremos bastante bien, como pasó en Hungría pues alcanzamos un rendimiento fuerte. En otras, sufriremos. Si hacemos una media quizá no lideremos esa parte de la tabla, pero estaremos bien colocados y no será algo lejano", apuntaba Mike Krack, ingeniero jefe en pista de Aston Martin.  El salto va de la mano de Honda. Que no penalizará en Holanda, según repiten desde el seno japonés. Y cuenta con la confianza de la fiabilidad que no apareció en los primeros compases del 2026. En su primer test -el corto filming day de 200 kilómetros en Hungría- lo validaron. "Confirmábamos que todo funcionaba y encontramos cosas interesantes en manejabilidad. Fue un buen progreso y sin problemas", comentaba Orihara. Su unidad de potencia, fundamentalmente, cambiará en la parte de combustión. "La potencia del motor era el punto débil y conseguimos una diferencia significativa en sus características", reportó. Sin miedo a vibraciones o a los grandes problemas de manejabilidad, los dos elementos negativos de la primera mitad del 2026. El paso al frente del paquete completo también aportará luz a Fernando Alonso, aunque ha repetido que su continuidad en la F1 no tendrá relación con el rendimiento del coche. Es una historia diferente, pero en Aston Martin siguen con su mensaje claro: esperan al piloto y creen en su continuidad. "Siempre ha comentado que decidirá el futuro en verano con lo que esperamos a su decisión en las próximas semanas. El objetivo es continuar con Fernando, y confiamos en alcanzar un acuerdo. Pero respetamos que tenga que tomar una decisión, así que esperamos por ello", lanzó Krack.  El asturiano, de momento, encontrará un AMR26B mejorado y con más pasos aerodinámicos. "Habrá cambios en el suelo y el alerón delantero con cosas que aprendimos en Hungría. No podemos probar mucho y tenemos que ser conscientes del foco en el lado del motor", radiografió el luxemburgués. Sin marcar una meta desmesurada en ese trabajo. "El inicio de año fue muy difícil, y ahora debemos ir paso a paso tomando el rumbo positivo. Habrá contratiempos, sí. Y habrá bajones o puntos álgidos. Pero debemos tomar perspectiva del progreso del curso y lo importante es ver esos pasos en fiabilidad y rendimiento", añadió.  Eso sí, todo dependerá de Honda. "Al mejorar rendimiento sabemos que habrá dificultades en la fiabilidad y cuando iniciamos el desarrollo ocurrió. Pero nos tomamos un tiempo largo, arreglamos los problemas y probamos en el banco dinámico que funcionaba. Creo que hemos alcanzado nuestro objetivo interno en fiabilidad y rendimiento", cerró Orihara. Sin descartar algún ajuste más en la segunda mitad de temporada. "Si encontramos algo bueno se valorará", sentenció.

articles.title: Alonso, el lugar que queda por confirmarse entre las estrellas
articles.standfirst: Tras las renovaciones de Sainz, Albon y Verstappen, poco asientos importantes restan por dilucidarse en 2027
articles.summary: Tras las renovaciones de Sainz, Albon y Verstappen, poco asientos importantes restan por dilucidarse en 2027
articles.body: Las tres renovaciones o extensiones de contrato que se han producido en las últimas horas dejan bastante clara la parrilla de 2027, con algunos huecos libres aún, pero con sólo uno realmente significativo entre las estrellas de la F1. La página web oficial del campeonato da como vacantes de dos asientos de Aston Martin, aunque el de Lance Stroll no tiene fecha ni plazos. Bien podría decir 'hasta que Lance quiera', al no depender del mercado por razones obvias. A su lado, Fernando Alonso debe decidir en los próximos días o semanas sin quiere renovar con los de Silverstone, aunque las declaraciones de confianza que parten desde el interior del equipo, la última de Mike Krack y antes de Adrian Newey, indican que su continuidad es la resolución más probable en estos momentos. Y seguramente por dos años más, hasta 2028. Mercedes, McLaren y Ferrari ya están con sus asientos cubiertos y podrían producirse extensiones adicionales, como la de Hamilton, en breve, pero parece que no habrá cambios. Con Max atado a Red Bull, ni Russell ni Piastri temen ya por una permuta de última hora. Al lado de Verstappen estará Isak Hadjar, como ya adelantó el director del equipo Laurent Mekies, "dado su rendimiento de este año. Es la decisión más lógica", adelantó el francés. Y en el resto de la parrilla, Cadillac F1 se da como cerrado con Bottas y Checo Pérez, cuando sólo el mexicano ha sido casi confirmado la semana pasada. En el lugar del finlandés se habla de varias opciones, con Colton Herta como principal candidato, si logra la Superlicencia de la FIA, que tiene complicada. Por último en Haas se ha abierto una especie de concurso de oposición para el asiento que dejará libre Ocon al final del año. Camara, Fornaroli, Hirakawa y luego Jack Doohan, serán probados tras Zandvoort y Madring en un TPC (coche de temporadas anteriores) y entre ellos se jugarán quién acompaña a Bearman en parrilla el próximo año.

articles.title: Verstappen: "Creo que podemos volver a la cumbre en los próximos años"
articles.standfirst: Max explica el motivo de sus cuatro años más con Red Bull y algunos detalles de las conversaciones
articles.summary: Max explica el motivo de sus cuatro años más con Red Bull y algunos detalles de las conversaciones
articles.body: Max Verstappen habló este jueves por primera vez con la prensa, unas horas después de que se anunciara su renovación por cuatro años más con Red Bull. Con la ironía y el doble sentido que le caracterizan, el tetracampeón de la F1 fue bombardeado a preguntas sobre los detalles.  "Sí, la verdad es que no ha sido una decisión estresante. Creo que era la decisión adecuada, me siento muy bien dentro del equipo y creo que podemos volver a la cumbre en los próximos años", resumía sobre los motivos de su firma. "La verdad es que se trataba de continuar en la Fórmula 1 o no, pero las normas han mejorado algo, y digamos que estoy dispuesto a convivir con ellas. Es de la vieja escuela y sin duda uno de los mejores circuitos del calendario, comparado con algunos otros, y no voy a dar nombres, a los que les falta algo de carácter, de personalidad. Y al ser neerlandés lo hizo ese poquito más especial", añadía. Me llevo bien con Oliver y con todos los gestores de Red Bull y estoy contento de ser parte de todo esto. Aunque es cierto que en los últimos meses he hablado de los planes y ideas del equipo de aquí en adelante y la verdad es que me lo han comunicado de manera cierta y transparente y eso me gusta. Me gusta lo que quieren conseguir y quiero seguir siendo parte de ello en el futuro", subrayaba.  Sobre los 15 años que va a estar ligado a Red Bull en la F1, Max bromeaba con el paralelismo de un matrimonio. "Bueno, me sirve de entrenamiento para mi propio matrimonio... Ya dije en su momento, cuando Dietrich (Mateschitz, fundador de la marca) estaba entre nosotros, que mi objetivo era competir contra el Bull para siempre, así que de momento vamos bien", explicaba. La posible llegada de los V8 en 2031, como ya se habla, será el siguiente momento para decidir en el caso de Verstappen. "No sé qué sucederá en 2031, aunque sin duda creo que ha sido más la dirección que va a tomar el deporte en ese momento", decía dejando claro lo que ha pesado en su decisión de seguir, que en la próxima era, que queda muy lejos aún.

articles.title: Max Verstappen: George Russell says his Mercedes seat 'never felt under threat' from Red Bull driver before contract announcement
articles.summary: Max Verstappen ended speculation over his future by signing a contract extension with Red Bull; the Dutchman had been linked with Mercedes and McLaren; watch Dutch Grand Prix practice live on Sky Sports F1 at 11.30am on Friday, with Sprint Qualifying following at 3.30pm
articles.body:
George Russell says his Mercedes seat "never felt under threat" from Max Verstappen before the Dutchman ended speculation over his future by signing a contract extension with Red Bull.

Verstappen has been repeatedly linked with Mercedes since soon after Lewis Hamilton announced in February 2024 that he was leaving the Silver Arrows to join Ferrari the following year.

Mercedes boss Toto Wolff initially appeared to be targeting Verstappen as a team-mate for Russell, but more recently the four-time world champion had been touted as a replacement for the Brit given the fine form that has taken his team-mate Kimi Antonelli top of the Drivers' Championship.

Following Red Bull's announcement on Thursday, ahead of this weekend's Dutch Grand Prix, that Verstappen has signed with the team until 2030, Russell suggested Mercedes' talks with the Dutchman's camps over the last couple of years may have been overblown.

Russell said: "It's only really a topic for us when we're sat in front of you guys in the press and you want to ask these questions and understand what's going on.

"It was always very clear from within Mercedes what the reality was over these past couple of years.

"Maybe those conversations were slightly more public than the conversations his team were having with the likes of McLaren, or Ferrari, or whoever else it may have been.

"That's the just the nature of the sport. Drivers talk with different teams, teams talk with different drivers. Everyone has to just see what their cards are.

"But my seat never felt under threat, and I felt 100 per cent security with Toto and the team, and that obviously now continues."

Norris: Would be cool to have Max as a team-mate one day

Reigning world champion Lando Norris reiterated that he would have welcomed Verstappen as his team-mate at McLaren had the Dutchman joined the reigning constructors' champions.

McLaren emerged as a possible alternative for Verstappen when it was revealed earlier this summer that the Woking squad had held talks with his camp.

The possibility of the switch also appeared to be made more plausible by the fact the Red Bull colleague he works most closely with, his race engineer Gianpiero Lambiase, has agreed to join McLaren.

Norris' status as reigning world champion led most to assume it would be his team-mate Oscar Piastri who would have made way for Verstappen if the move had happened.

"I never heard much more than what you guys did," Norris said.

"I welcome anyone to be my team-mate.

"Of course, a guy who has won as many world championships as he has, a guy who is as talented him would always be cool to have as a team-mate one day.

"But I know Oscar's my team-mate for still quite a while yet, I know nothing is changing."

articles.title: Los motivos de peso de Carlos Sainz: “Mi prioridad siempre fue Williams, no di importancia a los demás”
articles.standfirst: El español recalca a la pregunta de MARCA su compromiso total con el equipo de Grove tras firmar una renovación histórica
articles.summary: El español recalca a la pregunta de MARCA su compromiso total con el equipo de Grove tras firmar una renovación histórica
articles.body: Una sonrisa acompaña a Carlos Sainz en su caminar por el coqueto paddock de Zandvoort. En Holanda, donde llueve con frecuencia al borde de la playa y se espera un Gran Premio de los Países Bajos con incógnitas climáticas y buen espectáculo en pista, el español está revitalizado tras su flamante renovación. Max Verstappen le acompañó horas después en la mañana del jueves, pero la del 55 es más relevante si cabe. Por su nuevo estatus en la Fórmula 1 y en el deporte español, pues es uno de los deportistas mejores pagados (unos 30 millones anuales) más allá de los Carlos Alcaraz o Jon Rahm, que cuentan con una importante bolsa por premios en los torneos. Sainz no para su cabeza en su estatus galáctico, el método sigue siendo el mismo y pasa por el trabajo a destajo. Su foco es la pista y una declaración de intenciones al reforzar su relación con Williams. “Mi prioridad era quedarme. No forma parte de mi carácter decir que me quedaré aquí muchos años y bajarme del barco a la primera. Si digo que quiero pasar tiempo, tratando de ganar, salir no es el mensaje que quiero dejar ni llevarme. Además, hay una parte de liderazgo del proyecto y es importante para todos los que están diseñando el coche de 2027 porque el piloto confía”, cuenta a MARCA. Alza la voz como un jefe de filas, algo que nadie discute tras los podios de 2025 y la velocidad de 2026. “No di importancia a otros equipos, mi prioridad era encontrar la forma de seguir aquí”, añade. La flamante renovación va acompañada de razones. Una es el trabajo de Williams más allá de los problemas y existe con fichajes, inversión y proyectos que podrían cambiar el destino de Grove. “Son cosas que pasan detrás de las cámaras y son claves. Pasan por diseccionar el pasado, entender todos en lo que hemos fallado y ser autocríticos. Más allá de eso, saber qué principios básicos hay: no llegar tarde, en peso y con una base decente. Además, hay proyectos a corto y medio plazo que nos pueden ayudar a ser un equipo puntero. Todos lo han pasado, como McLaren que arrancó 2023 sin frenos delanteros y después ganaban. Pienso que somos capaces, aunque no sea tan rápido”, radiografía. En todo eso existe ese tratar de impedir la colección de errores que lastraron a Williams en este curso. Con un desarrollo temprano erróneo. Y un problema en la nueva generación de coches, pues su FW48 es un concepto estancado. “No se puede desarrollar mucho porque es fallido. Ni es rápido desde el principio, ni hay capacidad de evolucionar al ritmo de los demás”, detalla. Hace un curso la sensación era diferente. “Queda claro que algo no funciona. En 2025, evolucionamos porque entendíamos el reglamento y era un coche parecido al del resto, y de hecho dimos el mayor salto en rendimiento. Ahora hay una hoja en blanco, no acertamos y el año que viene es la oportunidad de darle la vuelta”, añade. En el corto plazo habrá el impulso de Azerbaiyán, pero Sainz es tajante al descartar cualquier mejora más radical. Foco en 2027, ante todo. “La mejora de Bakú nos puede acercar al top-10, pero estamos a 1,5 segundos de los Racing Bulls. Salvo que traigas como Aston un coche nuevo, no hay una mejora de segundo y medio. Así que debes traer un coche nuevo, pero este año no da tiempo”, lanza. Para que el proceso llegue a buen puerto, es otra clave la relación con Williams y su estructura. “Nos queremos, está claro. Después del año tan difícil que estamos teniendo, es importante demostrar esa confianza en el proyecto, entre uno y otro y que le vamos a dar otra oportunidad sabiendo el momento duro que pasamos y no esperábamos aunque sabíamos que habría baches”, cuenta. Con una tarea ya implantada. “Toca calmar aguas, enseñar mi confianza y empujar para que no ocurra”, cierra. Su pieza en el mercado ya queda colocada, Verstappen hizo lo propio y Alonso, el otro español, es la última estrella por decidir y confirmar que España seguirá con una pareja de pilotos en parrilla. “No es el mejor momento para España en la Fórmula 1. Los dos estamos en un proyecto en el que han fallado en el coche, pero si preguntas sí que se valora mucho a los españoles. Por ello podemos estar orgullosos. Nadie cuestiona a Fernando y en mí Williams confía de esta forma. Es una buena noticia para el deporte español”, sentencia.

articles.title: Un antiguo miembro de la Administración Trump entra con fuerza en Aston Martin F1
articles.standfirst: Robert Wood Johnson adquiere una participación minoritaria en el equipo que lidera Fernando Alonso en pista
articles.summary: Robert Wood Johnson adquiere una participación minoritaria en el equipo que lidera Fernando Alonso en pista
articles.body: Aston Martin sigue acumulando nombres importantes en su plana mayor para que el proyecto en la Fórmula 1 ascienda hacia la élite. Hay figuras en pista, con Fernando Alonso como jefe de filas; en la fábrica, liderada por Adrian Newey y también en los despachos. Al grupo comandado por Lawrence Stroll se suma Robert Wood Johnson, un antiguo miembro de la Administración Trump y embajador americano en el Reino Unido, que adquiere una participación minoritaria estratégica que le permitirá llegar al Consejo Directivo como uno de sus Vicepresidentes. Johnson, apodado como Woody en sus círculos, es una figura de prestigio político y empresarial. En las finanzas, es el heredero de la fortuna farmacéutica Johnson & Johnson, valorada en 651.210 millones de dólares estadounidenses como capitalización bursátil. En el terreno de los gobernantes, siempre se le ha vinculado al Partido Republicano y a la figura de Donald Trump, al que apoyó con firmeza en su primer mandato. A raíz de esa relación fue nombrado embajador americano en el Reino Unido dentro de un contexto peculiar, pues coincidió con sucesos claves como el Brexit.  Su vinculación con Aston Martin también obedece a sus fuertes inversiones deportivas. En el curso 2000 entró con fuerza y compró a los Jets junto a su hermano. No es la franquicia más exitosa en el campo, pero pertenece a la liga con más ingresos del planeta. Al mismo tiempo también tiene interés en el fútbol, con una participación en el Crystal Palace. articles.summary: Crystal Palace and New York Jets owner Woody Johnson has acquired a stake in the Aston Martin Formula 1 team; watch Dutch Grand Prix practice live on Sky Sports F1 at 11.30am on Friday, with Sprint Qualifying following at 3.30pm
articles.body:
American billionaire Woody Johnson has bought a minority stake in the Aston Martin Formula 1 team.

Johnson is the owner of NFL side the New York Jets and has a 43 per cent stake in Premier League side Crystal Palace.

His family business, Johnson & Johnson, is estimated to have a net valuation of $20.5b (£15.1b), as of June 2026.

Johnson will join the Aston Martin board of directors as vice chairman with immediate effect but his stake amount is currently unclear.

Lawrence Stroll currently owns 33 per cent of the team with the remaining 67 per cent split among several high-profile private equity firms, sovereign entities, and strategic investors.

An Aston Martin statement said: "The investment further demonstrates the strong appeal and positive momentum of the team at a time of unprecedented growth for Formula 1, particularly in the United States.

"Johnson's focus will be to support the team's commercial growth, especially in the United States, but he will not undertake any day-to-day management duties. As executive chairman and controlling shareholder, Lawrence Stroll will continue to manage and control the company."

Aston Martin are currently 10th in the Constructors' Championship after a poor first half of the season and start to their new power unit partnership with Honda.

A combination of Aston Martin starting work on their 2026 car late and Honda not meeting their targets for the new power unit regulations has put them on the back foot.

However, they brought an upgrade to the last race in Hungary and Honda have an engine upgrade at this weekend's Dutch Grand Prix.

Johnson said: "During my time as US Ambassador to the United Kingdom, I have developed a deep appreciation for Aston Martin's rich history, as well as Lawrence Stroll's strategic vision and entrepreneurial spirit.

"I am excited to partner with him and contribute to the continued development of the team, with the ambition of building an organisation capable of competing at the very highest level of the sport.

"We also share a commitment to growing the fanbase in the United States and introducing even more fans to the excitement of Formula 1."

articles.title: Dutch GP: Kimi Antonelli fastest from Lando Norris ahead of Sprint Qualifying as Formula 1 returns
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli outpaced Lando Norris in the sole practice session at the Dutch Grand Prix but Mercedes, McLaren and Ferrari appear to be closely matched; watch Sprint Qualifying later on Friday at 3.30pm with the Sprint itself on Saturday at 11am, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli was fastest from Lando Norris in the only practice session at the Dutch Grand Prix as Formula 1 returned from its summer break.

Antonelli, who is 50 points ahead of Lewis Hamilton in the Drivers' Championship, continued where he left off by showing great pace throughout practice to better Norris by 0.121s and asserted himself as favourite for Sprint Qualifying later on Friday at 3.30pm, live on Sky Sports F1.

McLaren have brought upgrades to the rear of the car to complete the package that helped Norris to victory last time out in Hungary and are set to contend at the front again with Mercedes and Ferrari.

  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream F1 with no contract 📺

Although Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc were fourth and fifth, Ferrari's new floor at Zandvoort appeared to be working well with both drivers within three tenths of Antonelli. The pair set their best lap times earlier than the Mercedes and McLarens, so, in theory, had a slower track.

George Russell was third and only 0.125s adrift of Antonelli as he looks to get his championship challenge back on track after a disappointing run of form before the summer break.

"It's tricky conditions. The wind is playing a factor and will continue to play a factor here," said Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok.

"But what was really interesting was that they were all within less than three tenths of a second at the top. That's really exciting for us as it shows that whatever work has gone on through the summer break, we've kind of carried on where we left off in Budapest.

"And I don't think we've seen the best of the Red Bulls in that session either yet."

Oscar Piastri was unable to match Norris and finished six tenths back while the newly re-signed Max Verstappen at Red Bull was only 11th.

Verstappen was visibly struggling with the balance of his car and faces the prospect of a challenging final home event as the Dutch Grand Prix does not have a contract beyond this year.

Liam Lawson has replaced Isack Hadjar this weekend at Red Bull after the Frenchman suffered a wrist injury last week and was 14th, while Yuki Tsunoda, who has replaced Lawson at Racing Bulls, was 17th.

Pierre Gasly is running a big upgrade package on his car and was eighth for Alpine, splitting Audi's Nico Hulkenberg in seventh and Gabriel Bortoleto in ninth.

Aston Martin have engine and aerodynamic upgrades in Zandvoort, so Fernando Alonso finished 12th and 1.5 seconds off the pace - the closest they have been this season - and will hope to translate that pace into Sprint Qualifying later on.

articles.title: NASCAR Legend Kurt Busch Opens Up on Brother Kyle's Death in Emotional Interview
articles.summary: NASCAR Hall of Famer Kurt Busch shared an account of his final moments with his late brother Kyle Busch in an emotional interview aired Friday on TODAY.
articles.body:
NASCAR Hall of Famer Kurt Busch shared an account of his final moments with his late brother Kyle Busch in an emotional interview aired Friday on TODAY.

Busch described gathering with other family members at the hospital after his brother suffered a medical emergency while using a racing simulator in May.

Kyle Busch died the next day after suffering what his family described as complications resulting from sepsis following pneumonia.

York Responded to Ad on Prostitution Site Before Arrest

"I was there at the hospital. I was there all day. Hoping, praying. Hoping for a turnaround," Busch told TODAY 's Craig Melvin.

Busch said his father, Tom Busch, did not go into the hospital room because he "wanted to remember him in the way he wanted to remember him."

During his own visit to the hospital room, Busch said he told his brother: "I got you, man. C'mon. I got you. I've got you, c'mon, be strong."

He wiped away tears as he added, "Just wasn't fair."

Busch told Melvin he has since been mentoring his brother's 11-year-old son Brexton Busch.

"He's a prodigy. He was on the gas even before all of this," Busch said about Brexton. "He can be a big star in the world of motorsports. He's 11, but he's already racing like an 18 year old, so it's time to be around a bit more."

About what he missed most about his brother, Busch said, "I loved, on track, him and I were carbon copies of each other.

"I just miss the on-track comradery. We could speak on track without saying a word... I miss the words that we never spoke to each other and the vibe that we had on track."

Kyle Busch competed in his final NASCAR Cup Series race 11 days before his death. The television broadcast said at the time he had been struggling with a sinus cold, per Steve Reed of the Associated Press.

He holds an all-time record 63 Cup wins along with 234 career victories across NASCAR's three national series and will be a lock to join his brother in the NASCAR Hall of Fame as soon as be becomes eligible for induction.

articles.title: Dutch GP: Lando Norris beats George Russell and Kimi Antonelli to Zandvoort pole with Lewis Hamilton in fifth
articles.summary: Lando Norris claimed his second consecutive pole with a superb Q3 lap at Zandvoort to see off the challenge from George Russell and Kimi Antonelli; watch the Dutch Grand Prix on Sunday at 2pm (build-up from 12.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Lando Norris beat Mercedes duo George Russell and Kimi Antonelli to pole position at the Dutch Grand Prix in a hectic end to qualifying.

Rain threatened to cause an anticlimax to qualifying but the track remained dry enough for the McLaren and Mercedes drivers to battle it out for top spot, with Norris edging out Russell by 0.102s and championship leader Antonelli by 0.133s.

Oscar Piastri was just 0.142s off in fourth in another tight session - a continuation of the trend throughout the Sprint weekend at Zandvoort - and sets up a fascinating race on Sunday when the lights go out at 2pm (build-up from 12.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1.

Norris won the last race before the summer break but is 90 points behind championship leader Antonelli, who opened up a 53-point lead in the title race following Saturday's Sprint as his closest challenger Lewis Hamilton struggled in the short race.

Russell won the Sprint and will look to make further inroads into his 56-point deficit to Antonelli, while Hamilton has work to do after only qualifying fifth.

The Ferrari drivers were the last to complete their laps in Q3 but they did not have the speed to challenge at the front. However, Hamilton outpaced Charles Leclerc for the first time in a competitive session this weekend.

Red Bull have also been disappointing at Max Verstappen's final home event - with the Dutch Grand Prix falling off the calendar after this year. Verstappen qualified seventh behind Leclerc and only one tenth ahead of Liam Lawson, who has replaced Isack Hadjar at Red Bull this weekend after the Frenchman suffered a wrist injury last week.

Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto continued his strong performances in ninth, as did Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad in 10th while his team-mate Yuki Tsunoda qualified 12th.

Aston Martin would have been expecting more from their engine and aerodynamic upgrades but both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll went out in Q1 in 18th and 19th.

How Norris saw off Mercedes challenge

Norris was pessimistic about his qualifying chances after being overtaken by Leclerc late in the Sprint on his way to third and pointed out McLaren's slow-speed corner weaknesses as something that was not solvable this weekend.

The team made some setup tweaks ahead of qualifying which gave both drivers more confidence as Piastri topped Q1 and Norris Q2.

Norris set the time to beat after the first Q3 runs with a 0.151s advantage over the field and the grid was under threat of being set as rain was on the way.

Everyone went out for their last efforts earlier than normal and the track remained dry enough for drivers to improve, so Antonelli briefly took pole position before Norris delivered a stunning lap which Russell was unable to beat.

"A little surprised, honestly. Just a decent lap. I was pushing because you have seen how close it is and one hundredth, two hundredths can make a big difference in the end," said Norris.

"But just a good turnaround from earlier today where I felt like we struggled a little bit. We felt very strong so the team did a good job, so credit to them on trying to get a little bit more out of the car.

"We had to try something because what we had before wasn't going to be enough. So we made some small changes, nothing that wasn't going to make us gain two tenths or one tenth even, but enough to maybe give me a bit more confidence. I felt like I could do that more today and it paid off."

Ferrari's new floor has not brought them any closer to the front but they could still be a threat in Sunday's race as Leclerc had impressive tyre degradation in the Sprint.

But, overtaking is set to be difficult so Ferrari will likely need to try something different strategically to get in among the McLaren and Mercedes battle.

Hamilton told Sky Sports F1: "I feel optimistic. Fifth is not the greatest but it could be far worse, so I'm grateful to be there but of course I wish I was up further ahead."

"However, our race pace was good in the Sprint. Charles had good race pace and the car is in a better place

"Hopefully with the right strategy and right execution I think hopefully we can challenge the cars ahead."

articles.summary: NASCAR Hall of Famer Jeff Gordon has won an individual race for the first time in 11 years.
articles.body:
NASCAR Hall of Famer Jeff Gordon has won an individual race for the first time in 11 years.

Gordon claimed two first-place finishes Saturday as the International Race of Champions returned to Washington, D.C. ahead of the Freedom 250 Grand Prix.

The 55-year-old drove both 10-lap races around the National Mall in a No. 24 car owned by Rick Hendrick.

Gordon's last individual first-place victory took place in 2015 with a Cup Series win at Martinsville Speedway. He retired from full-time racing following the 2015 season.

He returned to the top of the podium Saturday after passing Helio Castroneves to take the lead in the first race.

He overtook Castroneves and Tony Kanaan in the second race to sweep the day. Fellow NASCAR Hall of Famer Kurt Busch finished the competition in second place.

This marked the first street race for Gordon, who retired as NASCAR's all-time leader in road course wins.

The IROC event preceded the IndyCar Freedom 250, which is set to take place on the National Mall later Saturday afternoon.

articles.title: Dutch GP: Mercedes boss Toto Wolff defends decision to order George Russell to let team-mate Kimi Antonelli past in Zandvoort race
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli extended his world championship lead after finishing second in the Dutch Grand Prix; George Russell was third after letting his Mercedes team-mate through in the closing stages following a team order; Mercedes boss Toto Wolff says the call was "not a difficult decision"
articles.body:
Mercedes chief Toto Wolff insists it was "not a difficult decision" to order George Russell to allow team-mate Kimi Antonelli past him during the Dutch Grand Prix.

Championship leader Antonelli was running second to Lando Norris with 16 laps to go when Mercedes decided to pit the Italian for fresh tyres under a virtual safety car, bringing him out in third behind Russell.

It quickly became apparent that Antonelli didn't have the pace to challenge Norris for victory, but while he soon closed up on Russell, the difficulty of overtaking at Zandvoort meant there was no guarantee the Italian would be able to cruise past his team-mate.

However, Russell was told over the radio to allow Antonelli through into second, which would leave the Brit vulnerable to losing his place on the podium to Lewis Hamilton, on fresh tyres behind him with his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc in tow.

With the help of another VSC interruption, Russell did brilliantly to hold off Hamilton, but finishing behind Antonelli meant the gap between them at the top of the championship increased to 59 points.

Wolff told Sky Sports F1: "We had a free stop with Kimi - a team internal free stop - and George was incredibly at the end fighting and also fending off the Ferraris, who were on a much quicker car. Was really, really exceptional.

"That (the decision) looks difficult on the outside but not on the inside. It's a situation we discussed very often, also today in the morning 'we're not going to lose time fighting with each other and have two Ferraris breathing down our neck'.

"So, it would have been the other way around exactly the same. It plays no role who is ahead in the championship or not, it's just about protecting the best possible positions."

Wolff insisted that his focus has to be on the best result for the team, rather than worrying about the feelings of his drivers.

"I don't think Antonelli was anywhere near catching Norris," Wolff added.

"It was just the safest way in terms of scoring points. You could have played maybe leaving him in the Overtake Mode and then again, you are risking too much, you have two Ferraris all over you.

"So, it was some tough calls, but they need to be done when you want to fight for the constructors' and drivers' championship.

"This is how we are operating. Both drivers know that. We avoid situations like some other teams where it's not clearly talked like this.

"This is harsh times, there's 2,500 people who work for championships, and it's not one man's game. That's how we operate it the last 15 years."

Russell: Antonelli deserved second

Russell initially appeared to question the order over the radio as he asked whether Antonelli had a chance of catching Norris, but ultimately quickly followed the instruction.

Asked about his thought process at the time, Russell said: "We've always said as a team, when we're on different strategies, we're never going to fight and we're always going to invert, and that's always just been our sort of rules.

"And the fact is Kimi was ahead of me before the VSC and he tried something different to protect us as a team. He kind of copy-pasted what the Ferraris did.

"Could I have kept him behind? Maybe. But equally, it could have been a P5 as well.

"So, in the end, he deserved to be P2. I think P3 was a fair result for me."

Antonelli: George made my life a lot easier

Antonelli thanked Russell for obeying the team order but admitted he felt as though his strategy had put his team-mate at greater risk of losing a podium.

The 19-year-old took the lead by passing Norris at an early restart but was unable to match the McLaren driver's impressive pace once they switched to the hard tyre compound at the first round of pit stops.

Antonelli said: "It was a difficult second half (of the race) for me, especially in the last stint on the hards, just really struggling. Had little confidence in the car and, yeah, it was not easy.

"And then obviously we pitted, and also that was a bit tricky. But then also George, I have to thank him because he made my life a lot easier.

"But I still think probably could have stayed out and gone until the end with the same set because it put us a little bit at risk. Also, I feel we put George at risk with having to let me by and everything.

"But I still think, at the end of the day, it was a great team execution with how things were, and I think today P2 was the maximum we could have done because the pace of the McLarens, especially in the second half, was just too strong."

articles.title: Dutch Grand Prix: Lando Norris and McLaren 'don't have car' to fight for title
articles.summary: Lando Norris says he and McLaren "don't have the car I need to fight for a championship", despite a second consecutive win of the season at the Dutch Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Lando Norris says he and McLaren "don't have the car I need to fight for a championship", despite a second consecutive win to open the second half of the Formula 1 season.

The Briton's victory in the final Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort, following on from his first win of the season in Hungary last month, was of the highest calibre.

As such, it raises the prospect of the sort of championship fightback staged by Red Bull's Max Verstappen against Norris himself last year.

After this race last year, Norris' team-mate Oscar Piastri had a 34-point advantage over the Briton and 104 over Verstappen. Yet Verstappen, after one of the all-time great fightbacks, finished the season just two points behind Norris as he won the title in Abu Dhabi.

Norris' masterful victory in Zandvoort has left him 83 points off the lead, held by Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli, who he and McLaren passed on track after losing the lead at the chaotic start of the day.

Antonelli's team-mate George Russell is tied on points with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, 59 behind the Italian.

Norris beats Antonelli to claim final Dutch GP win Published 2 days ago

Norris beats Antonelli to claim final Dutch GP win

Russell impresses as Norris shines - driver ratings Published 2 days ago

Russell impresses as Norris shines - driver ratings

Mercedes lack money to develop car like rivals - Wolff Published 2 days ago

Mercedes lack money to develop car like rivals - Wolff

But while McLaren have made a major step forward with upgrades to their car that led to convincing wins in both Hungary and now the Netherlands, Norris believes that the car still has too many flaws to mount the sort of consistent attack Verstappen produced last year.

"I'm confident because we clearly have a strong car," he said. "We have a strong car in certain areas. It's not like last year where we were pretty good everywhere.

"We're very, very strong in high speed, and that's the place we've improved the car the most, is high-speed performance. No one matches us in high speed, and that's a good thing.

"My pace advantage to Mercedes in Turn Seven, Eight was crazy, but their advantage that they have to us in slow speed is also crazy.

"And therefore, I don't have the confidence to say, 'Yeah, I can easily fight for a championship for the rest of the season.'

"I know I've just won two races in a row and had two poles in a row, but at the minute I don't have the car I need to fight for a championship. And I know that's quite a big comment."

Norris' belief is based on his understanding that McLaren's slow-speed performance will be a handicap at the next race in Monza, and two races after that in Azerbaijan.

Both tracks are dominated by long straights, which penalise the McLaren's high drag compared to Mercedes, and have very few high-speed corners where the car's strength can compensate for its weaknesses in slow turns.

McLaren team principal Andrea Stella said: âIf we can confirm our improvements in Monza, then we can look with some optimism at the remainder of the season.â

Norris' victory in Zandvoort, built around an off-set strategy and devastating pace once the cars were on the hard tyres in the second stint, underlined the level at which he is now operating.

As impressive as Verstappen's revival was last year, Norris' own in the second half of the season was almost as good, as both made up ground on Piastri.

And Norris believes he has built on the progress he made in his driving after a difficult start to 2025 to perform on an even higher plane in 2026.

"I was driving at a high level the second half of last year," he said. "It's tough to say, but I do think it's a trickier car to drive this year in some ways. And I think you can see that because the gaps between team-mates are often bigger this year, I would say, than it was last year.

"I do believe I'm able to understand situations better, to understand the car in a better way. It's still just horrible to drive, but I'm doing a better job at just understanding this, relaying this to my team, figuring stuff out.

"So, it's not just I'm driving better on track. I'm certainly eliminating my weaknesses on track, and I don't have so many, but it's also how I work off the track. And for me, yesterday to today is a perfect example of the work we put in overnight transformed our race and gave me the opportunity to win."

Team principal Andrea Stella said he believed Norris was driving better than ever.

"Lando is driving and operating at a very high level," Stella said. "He's driving at the level of a world champion.

"What I like the most of his journey in Formula 1 is that he keeps improving.

"After the start of the 2025 season, something clicked, which is not only a single click, but it's a way of working with Lando, for Lando, and that we are adopting also on Oscar's side now in particular.

"This approach has led Lando to continuous improvements.

"It's almost like I see Lando stronger and stronger race by race. Because I think this weekend was nowhere near a weekend in which we could fight for the victory for granted, especially after having seen the performance in the sprint (in which Norris was passed by Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and finished third).

"But we invested in trying to understand where was the opportunity from a tyre exploitation point of view and car improvement.

"And then when you have conditions in which the car slides in the race, there's not much grip, then I think he is the master in these kind of conditions."

A couple of months ago, before the British Grand Prix, and before McLaren had won a race this season, Norris admitted in an interview with BBC Sport "a little bit" of frustration at not being able to defend the title he won last year.

So it's perhaps no surprise that now he appears to have at least an outside chance of making a fist of it, he is not making any presumptions.

"One race at a time," he said. "I know a lot of people say it now, but it's the truth of it. There's no point thinking that far ahead.

"Obviously, two great weekends, but there's still plenty of things we can do better, and we need to do better if we want to fight for a championship.

"It's still harder than I would like, and I don't want a bigger gap, so we have to keep working hard. There's still plenty of races, plenty of opportunity for everyone. So, keep my head down, keep working, and they'll keep coming."

McLaren's progress has come in the context of stagnation at Mercedes, whose lack of an upgrade to their car since Canada in May has led to them being caught by McLaren and Ferrari, a situation that has raised eyebrows among rival teams.

The next Mercedes upgrade is not due until the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia in four races' time.

For Antonelli - who also faces a grid penalty at his home race in Italy next time out because he needs to take a new engine that exceeds his allowance as a consequence of early-season reliability problems - it cannot come soon enough.

"Now as a team we need to find a little bit of time because McLaren have done a huge step," he said.

"So for sure, in this race, it's going to be more difficult, it's going to be challenging, but we're ready to do our best and to maximise every opportunity.

"And then hopefully it's going to be our turn to bring the package that's going to give us a little bit of the upper hand again."

articles.title: Lando Norris: Is McLaren driver now Kimi Antonelli's biggest threat for 2026 F1 world title after Dutch GP win?
articles.summary: Back-to-back wins for Lando Norris and McLaren has raised the spectre of the world champions yet having a significant say in this year's Drivers' Championship fight; watch the Italian Grand Prix at Monza live on Sky Sports F1 on September 4-6
articles.body:
While he won neither of the race formats across the Zandvoort Sprint weekend, Kimi Antonelli increased his overall world championship lead at the Dutch Grand Prix as Formula 1 returned from its summer break.

The Mercedes driver now leads both team-mate George Russell and Ferrari rival Lewis Hamilton by 59 points, the second-largest advantage Antonelli has enjoyed at the top of the Drivers' Championship so far this season.

But Antonelli's advantage over the driver now occupying fourth place in the standings was cut by a further eight points, following reigning champion Lando Norris' second successive Grand Prix victory, which moved him to within 83 points of the championship lead.

  • F1 2026 standings | F1 2026 calendar | F1 Gossip Column
  • Download the Sky Sports app for expert analysis, best video & more📱
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream F1 with no contract 📺

Norris became just the second driver after Antonelli to claim consecutive wins this season, with the McLaren driver's Zandvoort triumph coming after he overtook the championship leader on track. Antonelli had initially reclaimed the lead from Norris at the restart following the red flag triggered by Max Verstappen's heavy lap-one crash.

Yet does the result mean that Norris' hopes of retaining his world title, which seemed all-but over just a few races ago before McLaren brought a notable car upgrade to Budapest, are firmly back on?

Just how well is Norris driving?

Four weeks on from a supreme showing at the Hungarian Grand Prix, when he claimed the first Grand Prix pole and win of his world title defence, Norris was impressive again throughout the Zandvoort weekend on the sport's return to action.

But he was initially left frustrated on Saturday after finishing third in the Sprint.

Norris' concern centred on McLaren's long-run pace after Charles Leclerc overtook him with six laps remaining in the shorter-form race. The Ferrari driver was running on soft tyres that even he had expected to be past their best by that stage, making his ability to pull clear of Norris' medium-shod McLaren all the more concerning.

Norris later confirmed McLaren's single-lap pace was certainly strong by taking pole position for the main Grand Prix, but his 'celebrations' in parc ferme were noticeably muted.

Saturday's frustration made the nature of his win on Sunday all the sweeter.

Asked how highly he rated his 13th career triumph, Norris said: "Pretty high just from a point of just very well fought in many ways.

"More than that is, you know, the turnaround from yesterday to today. I was pretty disappointed yesterday. It kind of took a little bit of the fire out of me, seeing how much we struggled in the Sprint.

"I know it's just a Sprint, but, you know, every point matters and we just really didn't have the pace. I didn't have that something that gave me life inside the car.

"Last night we worked very, very hard. I spent a lot of time with my engineers to kind of understand what we could do better today, how to push more, save the tyres more, how to do everything in a better way than I've done and better than everyone else. And I certainly believe I did that today."

Having taken time to adapt to the complexities of F1's new regulations, and for McLaren to get on top of car and power-unit performance, Norris now feels back in a place to "make a difference".

"Of course I'm never one to over-talk about myself, normally always the complete opposite," he said.

"But for once I would give myself a little bit of credit that I feel like I'm doing a better job than everyone, and I think that can also make a difference."

Team principal Andrea Stella said after Sunday's race that Norris is "driving and operating at a very high level in absolute sense in relation to a Formula 1 world champion".

Stella added: "Lando is definitely now expressing a higher level of assertiveness as he drives. The manoeuvre on Antonelli is a really good demonstration of that.

"He's demonstrating more self confidence and the self-confidence sometimes is not demonstrated by being the most aggressive.

"Sometimes you are self-confident when you think like, 'you know what, I'm not going to have a fight now because I may lose in this fight, it's a very long race. See you at the end of the race'."

Does Norris now have the quickest car?

Although Antonelli, who turns 20 on Tuesday, has continued to barely put a foot wrong in the championship-leading Mercedes despite his inexperience, the team's early-season advantage over McLaren and Ferrari has been steadily eroded. Mercedes' relative lack of recent upgrades has allowed both rivals to close the gap, with McLaren in particular making significant gains in recent races.

articles.title: F1 Drive to Survive: Nueva temporada del icónico show, ahora con Checo Pérez en Cadillac, ¿cuándo se estrena y dónde ver?
articles.standfirst: La serie que cambió la forma de contar la Fórmula 1 regresará con una nueva entrega que seguirá las historias detrás de la temporada 2026.
articles.summary: La serie que cambió la forma de contar la Fórmula 1 regresará con una nueva entrega que seguirá las historias detrás de la temporada 2026.
articles.body: El rugido de los motores volverá a llegar a las pantallas con una nueva mirada al mundo de la Fórmula 1. Netflix confirmó que Formula 1: Drive to Survive tendrá temporada 9 en 2027, una entrega que seguirá los momentos más importantes del campeonato 2026, una campaña marcada por cambios históricos y nuevos protagonistas. La nueva temporada tendrá un atractivo especial para los aficionados mexicanos, ya que Sergio “Checo” Pérez formará parte de la parrilla con Cadillac F1 Team, la nueva escudería estadounidense que debutó en la máxima categoría del automovilismo. Aunque Netflix todavía no revela los episodios específicos, la presencia del piloto mexicano apunta a convertirse en una de las historias principales del documental. La novena temporada de Formula 1: Drive to Survive llegará a Netflix durante 2027, aunque la plataforma todavía no ha anunciado una fecha exacta de lanzamiento. Como ocurrió con entregas anteriores, la serie se estrenará después de que termine el campeonato de Fórmula 1 de 2026, con el objetivo de recopilar las historias más importantes del año dentro y fuera de la pista. Datos clave de la nueva temporada: Los productores ejecutivos James Gay-Rees y Paul Martin destacaron que esta nueva entrega buscará mostrar una visión más profunda del campeonato y entrar en espacios que normalmente no son visibles para los aficionados. La llegada de Checo Pérez a Cadillac será una de las narrativas más esperadas por los seguidores latinoamericanos. El mexicano regresará a la Fórmula 1 después de su etapa con Red Bull Racing, ahora con el reto de liderar el crecimiento de un proyecto completamente nuevo. La serie podría mostrar el proceso de adaptación del piloto mexicano, la construcción del equipo estadounidense y los desafíos de competir contra estructuras históricas como Ferrari, Mercedes y Red Bull. Además, la temporada 2026 ya cuenta con varias historias relevantes, como la evolución de nuevos talentos, la pelea por el campeonato y los cambios generados por una nueva era técnica dentro de la Fórmula 1. Entre los temas que podrían aparecer destacan: Los aficionados podrán disfrutar la temporada 9 de Formula 1: Drive to Survive exclusivamente en Netflix, la plataforma que ha transmitido todas las entregas anteriores del documental. Desde su estreno en 2019, la serie producida por Box to Box Films se convirtió en una pieza clave para acercar la Fórmula 1 a nuevos públicos, mostrando conflictos internos, estrategias de equipos y la presión que viven los pilotos durante una temporada completa. Con la incorporación de Cadillac y el regreso de Checo Pérez, la próxima edición promete una de las historias más atractivas para los seguidores mexicanos, quienes volverán a vivir la Fórmula 1 desde una perspectiva diferente, lejos de la bandera a cuadros.

articles.standfirst: Se ha dado a conocer que un alto mando de Cadillac no quería que el mexicano llegara al equipo de Cadillac.
articles.summary: Se ha dado a conocer que un alto mando de Cadillac no quería que el mexicano llegara al equipo de Cadillac.
articles.body: Sergio Pérez es uno de los mayores exponentes dentro de la Formula 1, el piloto ha pasado por escuderías como McLaren, Red Bull Racing y en la actualidad se encuentra con el conjunto de Cadillac, en el cual firmó un contrato por las temporadas 2026 y 2027, pero hace poco se dio a conocer que no todos estuvieron de acuerdo con la llegada del mexicano. Durante un episodio del podcast llamado "Desde el Paddock", el expiloto y amigo de Checo Pérez, Memo Rojas Jr. reveló que Graeme Lowdon, quien dejó recientemente su puesto al frente de Cadillac, habría sido uno de los principales obstáculos durante las negociaciones para incorporar al piloto mexicano. Lowdon se desempeñaba como director del equipo, su principal función fue liderar la entrada y la estructuración inicial de Cadillac en la máxima categoría del automovilismo, pero fue reemplazado por Marcin Budkowski a mediados de agosto de 2026. La principal razón por la que el ex director de la escudería estadounidense no quería que Checo se integrara al equipo, era por un nombre conocido dentro de la F1 y es Guanyu Zhou. Lowdon también ha trabajado como representante del piloto chino y de acuerdo con la versión compartida por Rojas en el podcast Desde el Paddock. La idea original era buscar que Zhou ocupara uno de los asientos disponibles en Cadillac, pero la escudería estadounidense tomó otra dirección. Checo fue elegido para acompañar a Valtteri Bottas durante la temporada debut del proyecto en Fórmula 1 y Zhou terminó incorporándose como piloto reserva. Checo Pérez y Guanyu Zhou han tenido caminos muy distintas en F1, por lo que vamos a revisar cómo han sido sus trayectorias dentro las carreras de monoplazas. Pérez debutó en 2011 con Sauber y a lo largo de su carrera, pasó por escuderías como McLaren, Force India, Racing Point y Red Bull, y después de un descanso durante 2025, regresó a la parrilla en 2026 con Cadillac. Número de Checo Pérez en F1: Por otro lado Zhou, debutó en 2022 con Alfa Romeo, equipo que posteriormente pasó a llamarse Stake F1 Team y Kick Sauber, en los cuales disputó tres temporadas como piloto titular, hasta 2024, para después pasar por Ferrari como piloto de reserva, en 2026 se integró a Cadillac en la misma condición. Número de Zhou en F1: Checo se ha convertido en una de las piezas principales para desarrollar el monoplaza y entender los problemas que han aparecido durante el año, debido a su gran trayectoria y experiencia dentro de la competición. Mientras que Zhou es un piloto sin tanta experiencia, pero podrá aprender mucho de sus compañeros de equipo, los cuales han demostrado que llegaron para consolidar este nuevo proyecto.

articles.summary: BBC Sport F1 correspondent Andrew Benson answers your latest questions after the Dutch Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Lando Norris beat championship leader Kimi Antonelli to claim his second win in a row with victoy at the Dutch Grand Prix.

Reigning world champion Norris moved up to fourth in the drivers' standings, 83 points adrift of Mercedes' Antonelli.

Four-time world champion Max Verstappen suffered heartbreak at his final home race when he crashed out heavily in the opening stages.

F1 correspondent Andrew Benson answers your questions after round 12 of the campaign in Zandvoort.

Is it fair to say the dominance of Mercedes is over? They haven't won a race since Spa-Francorchamps, and even then that victory wasn't consecutive. Are they focusing more now on scoring points than they are winning races?

There has been a very obvious shift in competitiveness at the front as the Formula 1 season has progressed.

Mercedes won the first six races of the season, but have won only two of the subsequent six.

Mercedes took 10 consecutive poles in the first 10 races, but have been beaten by McLaren's Lando Norris at the past two grands prix. And the fastest Mercedes was lower than second for the first time in Hungary, where Red Bull's Max Verstappen also lined up ahead of Kimi Antonelli.

Over the season as a whole so far, the Mercedes is the fastest car in qualifying by an average of 0.316 seconds over Ferrari, with McLaren a further 0.041secs adrift.

But what happens when you split that into the first six races and the next six?

Until the Canadian Grand Prix in late May, Mercedes were 0.453secs a lap faster than the next fastest team, which was McLaren at the time, and 0.489secs quicker than Ferrari.

Since Monaco, that gap has come down to 0.163secs over Ferrari and 0.270secs over McLaren. Red Bull's gap over the past six races is 0.353secs, whereas it was 0.813secs up to Canada.

There is a very obvious reason for this - Mercedes have upgraded their car less than their rivals. To a quite stark degree.

Each race, governing body the FIA issues a sheet showing the declared upgrades each team has brought to that race.

It's not a definitive list - teams don't have to put all the changes on that sheet, only the ones that are visible. But it gives an idea.

Since the start of the season, Mercedes have fitted a total of 24 new parts to their cars, compared with 37 for Red Bull, 38 for McLaren and 40 by Ferrari.

This is not a direct representation of relative spend, as some parts are more expensive than others.

But it's striking, for example, that Mercedes have also deployed fewer upgrades than Aston Martin, Alpine, Racing Bulls, Audi and Cadillac.

Even Haas, the team with the smallest budget on the grid, have had more upgrades than Mercedes, who have the equal lowest number with Williams.

This is all in the context of the budget cap, which is set at $215m (Â£170m) for all teams.

The question, obviously, is what is going on here?

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff says: "We haven't got the money to put developments on the car.

"We are trying to evenly split that through the season, based on our calculations of when we can bring the biggest updates and optimising the championship points. But we just can do what we can do."

How did the alleged improvements go on the Aston Martin? Is there any sign of improved performance? - Chris

Within the team, they were hoping that the Honda engine would reduce lap times by somewhere in the region of 0.3-0.5secs.

The weekend painted a confusing picture.

On the one hand, Fernando Alonso looked more competitive than ever before at various points.

But he qualified further away from pole in both positional and percentage terms than he had in Hungary.

There were, however, extenuating circumstances, in that he was 12th fastest before failing to improve on a messy final lap hindered by a sub-optimal 'prep' lap which left his tyres out of the 'window'. Without that, he probably would have progressed beyond the first session.

Nevertheless, that suggests the new Honda was little better than the old one. On the other hand, the new engine's drivability was definitely worse, which may have skewed the picture.

But then Alonso drove an outstanding race on a one-stop strategy to take ninth place, looking after tyres and measuring his pace with all the expertise and skill he has shown throughout his career to hold off two faster cars in Pierre Gasly's Alpine and Yuki Tsunoda's Racing Bull in the final stint.

Those are the first points Aston Martin have scored on merit all season.

As Alonso put it: "We scored one point in Monaco with nine DNFs (retirements). Today we scored two points with Max (Verstappen) DNF. It was well deserved."

Alonso said after the race that the team were planning a two-stop but changed during the race because they were stuck behind other cars.

"We are in traffic," he said. "We cannot use our potential. We are faster in the corners than the people in front of us and we are slower on the straights. We're stuck behind.

"So as soon as we have free track in front of us, we try to use it. Even if it's not the optimal performance and the optimal strategy, and it's what we did today."

On the car and engine upgrades, Alonso said: "Another step forward, especially on the chassis side.

"We brought four or five components here. Also the Budapest package was understood in the (summer) break. With all the data available after the race, we fine-tuned a little bit the set-up around that new spec. Plus the new parts. I think now we are optimising the chassis side and we are able to extract the maximum.

"The engine is more difficult. I don't think we can be black and white if we have more power or not.

The way the television broadcast was played out, it sounded as if Ferrari decided to pit Leclerc for fresh tyres to get him out of the way. He initially resisted that and did not come in, but then came in at the next call.

Team boss Frederic Vasseur addressed this after the race, in comments that were a little unclear.

First, he said, at that point, Ferrari were thinking of running Hamilton to the end, so they did not want him to push hard - but had not told him that was the case, because they wanted to keep the plan secret from their rivals.

As for Leclerc, Vasseur said they were "expecting him to pit" but then realised he was in danger of coming out in traffic.

Vasseur said: "Charles was supposed to pit, we extended one lap, and it was a kind of confusion, but I'm not worried about this. Everybody will be back in the briefing, they will have a clear picture about the race."

Some will inevitably say this was another example of Ferrari messing up their strategy, an accusation that is levelled at them quite often.

Vasseur said: "It's not so easy, but, if I look at the race now, my issue is that we didn't tell Lewis that we were expecting him to go to the end, and it was not a matter of (him) pushing (at that point)."

Did the delay cost Hamilton third? Hamilton thought so, but it's impossible to know whether he would have passed George Russell if he had had a lap or two more to try.

articles.summary: El equipo reconoce el trabajo que hizo el mexicano en Países Bajos
articles.body: A simple vista, Sergio Pérez y Cadillac siguen con los mismos problemas en la Fórmula 1, que es la falta de velocidad para competir a mitad de tabla por los puntos. Pero en el Gran Premio de Países Bajos dieron una muestra de cierta mejoría con respecto a la primera mitad de la temporada de F1 2026, pero con claridad de lo que se necesita para dar el salto competitivo. Justo el fin de semana en el Circuito de Zandvoort fue el primero de Marcin Budkowski como nuevo jefe de equipo y tras una pausa de cuatros semanas, la escudería de Estados Unidos celebra un buen stint en su segundo juego de neumáticos. Equipo: “Muy buen segundo stint. Muy bueno”. Pérez: “Sí, bien ejecutada la carrera. Una pena la posición 15, perdimos mucho tiempo en pits, muchos segundos ahí". Así fue la conversación al finalizar la carrera que ganó Lando Norris y que Checo Pérez terminó dos vueltas por detrás del líder y campeón mundial. El piloto de Guadalajara no pudo pasar del lugar 15 en la pista. De acuerdo con información de la Fórmula 1, en el GP de Países Bajos Sergio Pérez pasó 37.078 segundos en sus paradas para cambio de neumáticos, sin contar el tiempo que estuvieron en los boxes por el accidente de Max Verstappen. Comparado con el ganador de McLaren, Lando Norris pasó 35.626 segundos en los pits, una diferencia de 1.452, que equivale a 4.08 por ciento más del tiempo. Con respecto a Pierre Gasly, que fue el décimo lugar, la diferencia fue de 2.67%. No todo se resume al tiempo en pits, ya que Checo Pérez también ha manifestado que necesitan entre medio segundo y un segundo de velocidad por vuelta para poder pelear por los puntos y esos problemas son los que Cadillac y Budkowski deben solucionar.

articles.summary: La estadística que supera Sergio Pérez a 'Mad Max' tras el Gran Premio de Países Bajos
articles.body: A pesar de que Sergio Pérez ha tenido una temporada dura con Cadillac, en lo que es su vuelta a la Fórmula 1, hay una estadística en la que supera a Max Verstappen, aunque parezca difícil de creer. Ambos viven en polos opuestos en la F1, mientras Checo Pérez batalla con su MAC-26 para terminar las Carreras, 'Mad Max' tiene un auto más competitivo con Red Bull, aunque, éste tenga menor recorrido después de lo vivido en el Gran Premio de Países Bajos. De los 23 pilotos que han participado en alguna Carrera en la Temporada 2026 de Fórmula 1, Lewis Hamilton es el único que ha completado todas las vueltas (145), aunque, muy de cerca por Andrea Kimi Antonelli, quien sólo no pasó la bandera a cuadros en Barcelona tras abandonar en el ocaso por una falla mecánica en su Mercedes. Por su parte, destaca que Franco Colapinto está en el podio de más vueltas completadas, hasta el momento, en F1, con un total de 735 (98.66%), sólo 10 giros menos que el británico de Ferrari; eso sí, sin ningún retiro, y sólo no completándolas tras perder vueltas en carrera. Pero lo más notorio es la aparición de Checo Pérez en la posición 16 como el piloto con más giros realizados (587), a pesar de contar con un MAC-26, el más lento de la parrilla, y jamás haber concluido con la extensión completa de un gran premio, puesto que las veces que termina, lo hace con vueltas perdidas respecto al ganador. Una estadística en la que Sergio Pérez supera a Max Verstappen (578) por nueve vueltas después de que el neerlandés se accidentara en su gran premio de casa en Zadvoort el fin de semana pasado, y que lo tiene en el décimo octavo lugar. Eso sí, el piloto de Red Bull tiene más kilómetros recorridos (2,963 kms) que el mexicano (2,851 kms). De esta manera, el neerlandés sólo está por delante de más vueltas completadas que: Nico Hulkenberg, Isack Hadjar, Lance Stroll, Valtteri Bottas y Yuki Tsunoda, este último sólo con una participación, el GP de Países Bajos, después de que saliera al quite en Racing Bulls para suplir a Liam Lawson, que hizo lo propio con Isack Hadjar en Red Bull por una lesión en la muñeca.
